div.head: Dionysios bar Salibi's Literal Commentary on Job

div.ab: Further: A short literal commentary on the book of Job. May the writer be forgiven.

As an introduction to the second commentary in brevity which deals with the righteous Job we shall show to you the following: From Job man knows that searching which has God as object is natural (and) independent of the law and prophesy for without the scripture and the law he was known by God and he kept the natural law and loved God and he knew that God repays good with good and evil with adversity and not in this world but in the one hereafter, and because of this he took to behaving excellently and because of that world he did good deeds; and it can be deduced from the fact that he saw many in his age who were prosperous in earthly things but did not know God.

Moses wrote the book of him but did not arrange his book with his (Moses' other) works, because people say that he descended from Esau and not from Jacob. Others say that he did not write on his family because he belonged to the gentiles, the sons of Joqtan, as he did not write on the family of Melkisedeq. And those who say that he was from Esau say
that his name is Jobab. And he took an Arabic wife and she bore him a son and his name was called Hanan and the (father) of Job was of Zerah, and his mother was Basora and he is the fifth from Abraham. Job is the son of Zerah, son of Re'uel son of Isak son of Abraham.

Asaph the priest, the colleague of Ezra, and Aroz the chronicler, and Jacob of Edessa say that he belongs to the sons of Joqtan, the one who is the son of Eber and he is prior to Abraham and by a space of more than sixty years.

Moses composed the book so that the glory of the man and his prophecy should not remain hidden from the world and that it might make Israel ashamed that among the gentiles had risen a king and priest and prophet and that through Job he might put to shame those people of that age who did not know God, and that he might put to shame the rich ones who took delight in the opinion that they were good when they were rich and that those who were chastised might learn from him to endure pain and that everybody might learn that Satan exists who envies good things and they should beware of him.

Satan asked that he be allowed to tempt him. Because he could not make him sin by idolatry and lust, he wished to unnerve him through the destruction of his possessions and the death of his sons and disease. And that God might show Satan that Job was virtuous, neither because of riches and sons nor because he feared God by constraint but of his own free will he turned him over to Satan so that his servant might become victorious and the Evil one be put to shame. And for this reason he does not chastise the scoundrels and they end their lives amidst good things while the righteous ones are pursued and put to shame in the world. And we are of the opinion that he does not chastise those whom he knows chastisement will not correct; the righteous he chastises to show that not because he hates them does he chastise them but to teach that the good things which are here are nothing and he has eternal remuneration for easy circumstances as well as for adversity.

He chastises the righteous of whom he knows that they
will repent, he tries them knowing that they will not sin.

Job lived 255 years, eighty-five years before the affliction and after the affliction one hundred seventy. The Scripture says 248 as it did not reckon the seven (years) of the affliction because in them he is considered as dead. Seven were those of the affliction because of this: In six distresses and (even) in seven the Evil one shall not draw near unto you. (X.19)

There was one man, i.e., he says one to teach that there were not others like him. In the land of Us, i.e., the son of Shem. The boundary of his land is from the boundary of the land of Egypt until Damascus. A simple-hearted man, i.e., by reason of a diligent search for God for inasmuch as he was known to God he did not investigate nature in general but the nature (of God); but as one who praised and eulogized God, he did not trouble himself with examining and therefore he is called simple-hearted. And righteous, i.e., through all the virtues and the natural law. And he feared God, i.e.,
naturally from the fear of the judgment. He eschewed evil, i.e., in the hope of remuneration. He (Moses) mentioned the merits before the sons because he was glorified and adorned; and the sons before the possessions because they were nearer according to nature. He mentions the possessions to make known how much wealth he possessed and it was a spur to good deeds for him and not to sin.

He was greater than the sons of the East, i.e. the excellent ones of his age; and than all those who lived east of him. They used to make a banquet, i.e., he accustomed his sons to eat and drink together that he might unite them in love and that they might become virtuous, modest, sober, and honorable, for with strangers they did not learn excellent habits as they did with one another. And he sanctified them, i.e., he offered sacrifices for them, not because they had sinned actual sins but in case they should have sinned in their unrevealed thoughts. Perhaps my sons have thought, i.e., he knew that thoughts spring up from the heart. And the purgation he performed not according to the law but like the apostles. And he purified with sacrifices like a priest in token of his ministry. He knew that evil thoughts are sown in
the hearts of those who eat and drink, for behold, Moses also said to the people: Beware lest thou eat and drink and forget the Lord thy God. (comp. Deut. VIII. 10-11)

And it happened one day that the sons of God came, i.e., in the Septuagint version is written that the angels came, and Mar Johannes says that they are angels, those; namely, who have power over the earth and the movement of the elements, and of the winds (souls), and who show their works as they fulfill those things with which they have been charged for they are sent out for service.

The Accuser -- It is not that he rose and came like the angels; but he watches (stands regularly) in the earth in order to harm the human beings and he associates from time to time with the angels; but they take care of the service and guarding while he (takes care of) damaging and ruining. Others (say that) the sons of God are the just and righteous ones and (that) they came to Job for the reason of diligent search for God and adoration of him. They are called sons of God like the sons of Seth are called thus because of their excellency and also the priests are called sons of God according to (the verse) I have said that ye are gods (comp. Ioh. X.34; Ps. 82.6)
That Satan came and stood among them (comp. I. 5), i.e., as he stood at the right hand of Joshua the son of Jozadek in order to oppose him (Sach.III.1f.) and as one who misleads and tempts man.

Those (words) which are written; The Lord said to Satan and Satan answered ......... There was no questioning there and no answering; for, (1) the Lord does not need to ask, knowing everything beforehand; (2) nor does he (God) consider Satan worthy to be asked; (3) on the contrary he (God) speaks to those who fear him and keep his commandments, but it is figurative style of the narrative (used) for our sake.

I have walked about the earth, i.e., All the kingdoms have been handed over to me and nobody has escaped me free of sin except Job. (This was) because the divine protection restrained Satan from doing harm to him. And the Scripture uses questioning and answering according to the habit of human speech in order to show the craftiness of the accuser.

Does Job fear God for nothing? i.e., the Evil one spoke as if to God that he, (Job) did not love God of his own free will but for the sake of wealth. And when the Evil one began to draw near a little to the property as a temptation he was not held back and he felt at once that the protection of Job was abolished and in one day he destroyed everything and
also to himself did he draw near that day with the intention of destroying (him) but was held back by the protection as it is indicated by the sentences (lit. and it is known by this) Do not stretch out your hand against him. Spare himself (comp. II,6).
He spared messengers from the temptations in order that they might bring report to Job and later on he destroyed also them. And others say that demons imitated his servants and came and told him.

The fire of God fell down from heaven, i.e., those demons also brought down the fire from somewhere (lit. from where they brought it down) and it set fire to the sheep and the shepherds and consumed them and they (the demons) came and told him that God had done this so as to urge him to blasphemy: See, thy God whom thou trusted he has destroyed thee. And because of the extension or spirituality of the demons they were able to destroy at the same time all the people as well as the buildings like they did to the swine (comp. Matt. VIII,32) and like the angels who brought down fire on Sodoma (comp. Gen. XIX).
He spared his wife, not because he pitied her but that she might become to him an instrument for evil, like he made Adam sin through Eve thus (he intended to seduce) Job through his wife.

She said to him, Curse God and die. Johannes says that the wife was excellent and (that) the accuser imitated his wife and spoke this. And it was God's will that his wife should not perish lest he should take another one; as Job was one also his wife should be one, as Adam was one also Eve was one; in this is blame of marrying several times. His wife escaped also in order that she might wait on him and feed him. Further, she did not perish that the Evil one should not rejoice in that she died blaspheming, and she suffered with Job and it is meet that she who suffered with him should rejoice in the good (which came) to him. Job rose and rent his mantle, i.e., as if he would even add to that which harmed him.

Naked I went out, i.e., without wealth and property and without sins; naked I shall return, i.e., to Sheol without property and iniquity like that which Paul said: Nothing we have brought into the world nor shall we bring out (anything) from it (I Timothy 6.7)

That I delivered him over, to thee to bodily destruction so that you might destroy him; and this was without cause because he had not committed any since because of which he should be delivered over to bodily destruction in order that he might recreate his soul.

Satan answered, i.e., (through speaking) with the demons his companions and with himself he spoke with God. When
he saw that Job had not comitted blasphemy by reason of those things which had been done unto him, he wanted to pretend to him (God) that as far as those things were concerned so did he (Job) not actually suffer (from) them and so he had not committed blasphemy for he who is free from pain remains in his body and for this reason he said: Everything that a man hath will he give for, i.e., it annoyed him more that God guarded him so that he did not die than that he guarded him so that he did not commit blasphemy.

Because the Lord knew that he would not commit blasphemy even when he was smitten on his body he delivered him over to Satan that he might draw near and smite, being not restrained any more by the protection and he smote him with unsurpassable pain.

Spare his soul, i.e., he did not give him power to smite him thus that his soul was separated from his body and he was grieved for this reason. Further Spare his soul, i.e., even if thou smitest him from without without with sore ulcers and from within sowest evil in him and kindlest wrath thou shalt not have power to destroy his intellect.

He sat upon the ashes, i.e., first, being humiliated; second, because the stinking flux of the disease so that it
was consumed by the ashes (Text in strolling around) and did not stay upon the ground and he was forced to change (his) place when his flux became more intense for he was not able to rise and sit down and he had no slaves or maids to carry him.

Curse God and die. This was by the bewitchment of the Evil one; she expected that whosoever cursed the name of God instantly would die. Curse and die that thou mayest be delivered from the trial; for the simple (woman) had not experienced the longanimity of God whom many curse and who suffers it without killing (them). Further Curse God and die, i.e., that even if he did not actually die he would be dead in sin which the accuser would also like.

Shall we not receive evil from him? i.e., God had not brought the evil nor does he (see the author of the book of Job) say that he (God) was the cause (of it) but we may say (in a general way) that it was from him because he could have debarred it. In another way evils from him because although outwardly (lit. according to what was seen) they hurt and caused pain to the body, inwardly (lit. according to what is known) they were benefactions through which he himself became victorious, also because he became the cause for victory for many. His friends, i.e., princes and kings who were related to him; and they came to comfort him but they knew him not because the forms of his body had been destroyed by the trial.

Sprinkling dust toward heaven, i.e., according to the custom of the place. They showed the skillful ones of the people that it (the dust) belonged to it (the heaven) also when it was punished (text has was dispersed). Perhaps a man will say: When they were kings why did they not lift him up and bring him to their houses and take care of him and heal him? We are, however, of the opinion that he did not wish that they should do this to him because he did not believe that he could flee from the affliction and take refuge with men rather than with God. Also nobody was able to draw near to him or to inhale his odor because of the vehement stink of the ulcers. The accuser also saw to it that they became hardened against him lest anybody should comfort (him).

And until the skull, i.e., he left the skull (the brain) alone as the organ of mental power. And until the skull, not that he(Satan) especially cared for his intellect but because when the mental powers were kept (intact) they would become to him a cause of (urger to) blasphemy on his part, and (also) for the sake of his (Satan's) victory his (Job's) reason was not harmed for if the plague had reached his mental power he would have become an idiot and if he (then) should utter blasphemy he would have been found guiltless.

And he sat outside because he should endure cold and heat and that it might become manifest to everybody that those
things which befell him did not befall him because of sin; and if he had lived in the house the atmosphere in it would have become foul from the vehemence of the stink and his mental powers would have been harmed.

He cursed the day on which he was born, i.e., Satan smote him with ulcers from without and sowed evil thoughts from within and stirred up anger that Job should commit blasphemy but he (Job) made an outlet for the anger in action and he did not curse God nor the friends but (he cursed) something (that was) material and without (individual) existence. Those who suffer bitter days may oppress it, i.e., those who are in pain like me and who curse the day on which they were born.

May the cursed ones of the day curse it, i.e., those who enter Gehenna, those who have been accursed on that day and enter Gehenna with the accuser, he who is called Leviathan. Those who are ready to wake up Leviathan, i.e., Leviathan, the furious bitter judgment (read Judges ?) which those are ready to wake up for the day of torment; by their clamour, they will wake up the tribe of righteousness and they curse the day of their birth.

The cursers of the day, he calls the angels; he says that with him they shall curse the day. That those (are the ones) who are ready to wake up Leviathan (means) physically: when they lift him (Leviathan) up (text: demonstrate to it)
in the clouds that he can become the food of a strong people lest he should putrefy and the sea become foul by reason of him if the corpse remained in it. Also the animals which are
in it and the fishes would die and the sea would not be navigable to men. Spiritually they are the angels who drive together the demons to the torment. Further (they are) the righteous ones whose contempt is well-grounded, who are ready to be called to account by the Evil one whom he (the author of the book) calls Leviathan or (it may mean) that those should curse it (the day) as a retribution (vengeance) for sins who burn for days of evil deeds in the fire which is guarded by Leviathan. There the oppressors are at peace, i.e., he speaks of the time of death until the resurrection because there is no good thing for the righteous and not either any adversity for the oppressors. For (not until) in the judgment are the two parties retributed.

Before my bread my groan entered, i.e., I remembered the hungry who had no bread and I used to sigh and weep for them. And my roarings are poured out like water, i.e., for the sake of the poor who were in need.

Because the thing I greatly feared has come upon me, i.e., he knew that righteousness entails the hostility of the envious, and uprightness the temptations of the accuser and he feared that his righteousness might be destroyed; and just like the possessor of gold is afraid that his possession might perish, thus he, who possesses righteousness (is afraid) that it might be stolen from him until it enters before God as a sac
rifice. I had no rest nor was I idle (lit. kept Sabbath), i.e., from doing excellent and righteous deeds.

And I did not rest but punishment came, i.e., the envy of the accuser toward the excellent deeds, and that envy put me in this punishment, (which consists of); (1) the perishing of my sons and property and, (2) of the ulcers.
Elifaz said: If I assay to speak with you, will you become irked? i.e., will you be grieved, not have longanimity and get angry?

Thou hast instructed many, i.e., you have consoled them in their temptations, teaching that on the ways of righteousness are steadily temptations. And thou hast strengthened weak hands, i.e., with faith.
Did not thy words upholden the weak ones? i.e., those who were weak in temptations and in faith. When they see you (now) that you are weary and disgusted will they not repudiate your words?

It has come upon thee and thou faintest, i.e., you have grown weak and been defeated, and you used to heal others (but) yourself you cannot heal. This thy fear is thy reproach, i.e., because you cursed the day on which you were born.

Thy confidence and the uprightness of thy soul is thy judge, Who is the innocent who perished? i.e., By
this he rebukes him: If you had been innocent you would not have been put to shame.
Even as I have seen them that plow with sin, i.e., the rascals who oppress, and it is said that they are repaid according to their sins.
They are deprived of the breath, i.e., that which God breathed into them; and they become like dust and then they are judged with wrath.

The groan of the lion, i.e., he compares Job to a lion and to its teeth his riches and his power and to sons the whelps of a lioness and like the power of the lions depart from them when their teeth are broken, and nobody fears them, thus also you have come to naught because of the wanting of your bread and the scantiness of your table and your possessions and your riches have perished.

To me was answered a word, i.e. it concerns a revelation in a dream and from a vision I have (lit. I have found) those things which I say. And if this was really so it must have been from the accuser who, likewise as he wished to make him (Job) sin through his wife, also made the friends act so as to seduce, that he might inflame the righteous one.
In the falling of a deep sleep, i.e., in the sweetness of sleep. My bones were shaked, i.e., from fear of the one who called.
And a wind he let pass before my face, i.e., the cloud of slumber was dispersed from before me. And the hair stood up, i.e., by reason of the voice in the vision.

I rose up but I could not discern, i.e., I have not seen who woke me up but suddenly I heard somebody speaking, saying: Should mortal man be (considered) more just than God?, i.e., mortal man cannot be more just than God nor be more pure.

Yonder does not put his trust in his servants, and in his angels, i.e., to be taken in the plain sense (of the words) and this is because they (the angels) are as yet flexible and they have not been perfected in excellence.

He charges with wondering, i.e., over his works, and his administration, and his infinite nature, and his invisibility. And if even the angels cannot be compared to his righteousness -- and that although they help in his providence -- and (to) his purity. Those who live in houses of clay which are perfected from dust, i.e., in bodies (text: in the body) which were moulded out of clay and perfected as the ornament of the creation, how could they imagine that they could be considered righteous like God?

They are crushed in front of the vapour, i.e., before death, before the judge, before the torment. From morning to evening they are crushed, i.e., from when sin began and man sinned and until the end of the world because of: In
the sweat of they face (etc.), and they are punished by temptations and pains and death. That they should not be established as inhabitants forever, i.e., in this world they shall not live forever. And perish, i.e., from God because of their evil nature for it is much better that they die and are destroyed than that evil should be immortal.

Lo! does not their excellent things pass away? i.e., this world and its riches. Further, their excellent things (is) the paradise and the life. And the rest of them, amidst them they die, i.e., the sinners which are among them and the rascals, are dead in sin. And not with wisdom, i.e., because if they had been wise they would have died according to nature and the transgression of the command (Gen. III.22) yet finding life in spirit and righteousness (lit. however, in spirit and righteousness life would have been found).
Cry, I pray, if there is anybody who shall answer thee, i.e.,are there among the just and the holy ones any who will answer thee? Who shall answer you or who agrees to those words which you speak?
Because wrath and envy kills the fool, i.e., beware of wrath and envy lest they shall kill you like the fool.

And they are humiliated in the gate, i.e., when they go around from gate to gate as beggars to beg bread. Further, they are humiliated in the gate of the kingdom according to: Our Lord has opened for us.

What he has reaped the hungry eateth up, i.e., what he has reaped another eats. Further, what he has reaped,
i.e., in this world they eat but they are not satisfied and they drink and their soul is not satisfied and in the one which is to come torment like this is even more abundant.
Because from the dust does not come out, i.e., from the humble ones and the just ones. Fraud, i.e., iniquity, this on the contrary radiates and goes forth from the evil ones and the calumniators.

Because man was borne to toil, i.e., he has been placed in this world for the sake of toil and work of (toward) excellency, and he should not consider this world a place of delights as David says: In the toil of man they do not exist.

And the birds lift up the wings, i.e., the big fellows who get haughty (lit. exalt themselves) and rob and are arrogant and prey like eagles. But I will trail, i.e., by this he teaches that from his works he knows him.

Who does great deeds without end and miracles, i.e., those of the creation, those by the hand of Moses, (those) by the hand of Christ. He has given rain. This is allegorical. Upon the earth, i.e., the human heart. And he sendeth water upon the streets, i.e., the bath of reconciliation to those who are filthy by (reason of) sins like the streets of cities are filthy.
To place the low ones in the high, i.e., in heaven, the low ones: by sin, or by evil, or by humility.

And the humble ones are strengthened, i.e., like this: Happy are the humble and the poor of spirit. He disappointeth the devices of the crafty, i.e., of the demons and the crafty ones of the world. So that their hands can not do wisdom, i.e., the world has not profited by their wisdom, nor were their doctrines able to destroy the Evangel.

And the intelligence of the shrewd ones,i.e., the demons and the scribes of the Jews and the children of Israel when they crucified the Messiah. In the daytime they grope, i.e., it became dark to them at the time on which all the world was illuminated.

He saves from the sword, i.e., the apostles -- those he calls the poor -- from the tongue and the hand of the Jews, or the gentiles from the demons. And to the poor shall be hope, i.e., Christ, the life, the resurrection. And he stoppeth the mouth of the wicked one, i.e., Satan and the Jewish people.

Happy is the man whom he shall correct, i.e., after these words he turns to admonishing Job and his words concern the good which God will give to whomsoever suffers his correction and allows himself to be educated by him.

He breaks and binds up, i.e., that if he is patient he will get the reward and his former state is going to come
back to him. In six troubles, etc., and From the beasts of the plain thou shalt not fear, i.e., of the demons who were the cause of those things. Because with the stones of the field thy pact shall be, i.e., he will make you firm like the stony rocks and make you stand so that no more you shall be afraid of them. And the beasts of the plain shall be at peace with thee, i.e., the demons who have battled with you shall give up to you the victory. And thou shalt know that thy tent shall be at peace, i.e., he puts in order your house like before. And thou shalt return to thine habitation, i.e., to your house, a return without sin to thy former estate (a return which is not from the punishment of any previous sin).

And thou shalt enter thy grave in peace, i.e., full of days. As a shock of corn comes in his season, i.e., you will enter the grave like a deposit (the thesaurus) and like a shock of corn (the storehouse) (both of) which are going to be revealed again; and to go up from the earth in which it was buried.
This we have examined, i.e., I have examined. And thus we have heard it, i.e., that there is a resurrection. And you, know yourself(?), i.e., Job, revert you Job.

O, that my punishment were weighed, i.e., that also my trials were by measures. Because it is now harder than
the sand of the sea, i.e., my trials. Therefore, my words are held back, i.e., because I have been smitten by God and nobody believes that without having acted foolishly, lo! I am punished by God.

The terrors of God set themselves in array against me, i.e., his forces. In another way: I am horrified at my complaint against God for nobody confirms my (view) that I may have been punished (lit. destroyed) without cause, because everybody testifies that God is just and does not smite those who have not sinned.

Does the wild ass bray when he has grass or loweth the ox over the fodder? i.e., this does not seek grass nor yonder food and like these do not shun those (the food) because they (the food) are life for them, thus I would not either have cried and asked for death and cursed the day of my birth if not my soul had been bitter and sick of the plentitude of strifes, and you O, Elifaz, whose grass is full and fine, you snort upon the grass like the wild ass and you are quiet and do not cry and you are not in pain and do not lament, I however, am like an ox that is deprived of fodder and I lament. Thus I lament because if those things of which I have been deprived because of the pains of my members.

O, that I might have my request, i.e., that my former
state would return and I might complete (my life) in the strength of God. For I have not forsaken the words of the Holy one, i.e., I know that not because of sin, O Lord, have those (the pains) befallen me (the text has: That not by reason of sin or by reason of (from) the Lord have those etc.).

What is my strength that I should endure? i.e., because my afflictions surpass strength. And what is my future that I should be longsuffering? i.e, not as a blasphemy does he say thus but because he wishes to know the future remuneration for these (trials) as that he may procure longanimity from hope. However, I am not stone or brass but suffering and fragile flesh. And because I am far from his help, lo! I am in pain.

He who holds back peace from his neighbors abandons the fear of the supreme one, i.e., this he said to the one who rebuked and did not talk peace to him but blamed him. Because of his sins, lo, he is punished and not is this one righteous and that is evident from what has followed.

My brethren have dealt deceitfully like brooks and like ......, i.e., they are destitute of love like brooks which have no heat. Who used to fear the ice, upon them is much snow, i.e., that likewise as the brook which was frozen and become liquid and becomes soft by the change of the atmosphere thus their friendship toward me; for the firmness of their love has been dissolved by reason of my trials. In another
way: that like a brook and a stream are filled in the time of winter thus you used to be attracted to me in my wealth and like they (the brooks) are evacuated in the time of heat thus you depart from me in my trials. Who used to fear the ice, i.e., this is that fear (the verb is the one which is derived from fear).

They looked at the roads to Teiman and the highways to Sheba; by those he indicates (allegorically) wealth, for they were put to shame by something which was confided to them, because everything perishes.

Before you see something terrible you are afraid, i.e., it corresponds to that which Elifaz (said) that you called me an object of fear and horror. If you being integer are horrified, how much more ought you then to fear that horror in which I am standing. Further, Before you have seen, i.e., without having seen in me anything worthy of reproof you have attacked me. If you have blamed upon me, O Elifaz, that I have been afraid while my trial was hard and (if) you have said to me: Thy fear it is which blames thee, how much ought you yourself (then) to be blamed because you were afraid and feared while your body was not shaken and the trial had not reached you.

If it were that I had said to you: Give to me, i.e.,
If I had admonished you it would have been right that I should be reproved by you. Teach me and I shall hold my tongue, i.e., If I have not said one of those (things) why is then my word of truth pursued by you?

Yea, ye overwhelm the orphan (or the childless), i.e., orphan he calls him(self) because he is bereft of so much, and it would have been becoming that they should not have rebuked him but that they should have consoled him; but because he did not wish to blame them as evildoers he said: Be pursuaded and see, i.e., Be converted now and establish within yourselves a right opinion.
Be converted I pray and be victorious, i.e., hear me and listen to me and if it be that my mouth does not speak the truth, lo, you are victorious.

Lo, an appointed time is to man on earth, i.e., this was known that in heaven man shall not be for a (limited space of) time but eternally. And they are like the days of a hireling, i.e., to that end he was placed in this world; and according to his work he receives his wages like this: A lord went out to hire workmen, (Matt. 20.1-16). Further, Lo, an appointed time is to man on earth, i.e., a short time you and I serve upon earth(lit. a short time is served by me
and you), therefore, do not sin because death is to come and everybody is repaid according to his actions.

Thus I have inherited empty months and nights ...., i.e., my works of righteousness were not reckoned as having priority against the trials so that I have not been repaid according to my labor. If I lie down, i.e., I have not troubled the Lord about the end nor did care for the coming day prevail in me. Further, If I lie down, i.e, those long troubles passed away from me. Worrying (N.E. 298) about the day to come was not with me and I did not worry until morning, i.e., not even when awake I have designed during the time destined for sleep.

My flesh clothed itself in vermin, i.e., because I used to contemplate over death and vermin and worms and the return to dust; and instead of that I lay down and arose I contemplated these (matters). And thereafter my days were swifter than a weaver's shuttle, i.e., I was contemplating that my days are not longer than a woof which is about to be cut, for my soul like a skillful (female) weaver cuts quickly the days. And they perish because there is no hope, i.e., and this is because there is no hope of eternal rest for man in this world and therefore I used to hasten toward the exit. Further, They perish, i.e., because there was no hope of the
the one who delivers from trials.

He remembered that the spirit lives, i.e., (spirit means) the soul as rational (and) intelligent; that he is alive by a miracle. Further, He remembered, i.e., as yet the soul is (still) in the body although (the body is almost) dead by reason of pains, it has not yet been separated from it.

My eye turned, i.e., it was turned to see benefactions and I know that God is not going to gladden Satan with me because I shall be relieved. And your eyes be upon me and it is not I, i.e., you, O, Elifaz, look at me and after a little while you will see that it is not I, the one, who is now degraded and has been thrown upon the dung.

But as the cloud is consumed and vanishes away, thus he that goes down, i.e., according to your opinion I shall not go out of these (plagues). However, I shall go (even) from Sheol to life and not only from the trials but also from death.

Nor will I hesitate in using my mouth, i.e., consequently I will not retain my mouth from (speaking against) mendacious talk. I will speak in the anguish of my spirit, i.e., all that which comes to my mouth, blasphemy, murmur, for if I am not found (do not exist) later on what good is it then that I have guarded my mouth from uttering blasphemy and curses.

Am I a sea or a sea-monster that thou settest guard over me? i.e., the sea you have fettered with the sand and
over the sea-monster you have placed the cloud as a guard, upon me thou hast placed the trial; and the sea has a guard, the sand, and the sea has no pain. And the sea-monstor, you lift in a cloud in order that its stink when it dies in the sea shell not hit upon the islands and spoil the air and kill the human beings and the fishes through the rank of its corpse, and it is thrown into certain regions according to You have given it as food to a hard people. (Ps. 74.13-14) Thus also me, like (you would do to) a rebel you have fettered my members in pains.

Because I have said that you would comfort me, i.e., I have thought in my pains that I might hope that you were going to comfort me. Lo, you have scared me in my dreams, i.e., You Elifaz! He says to him: Not even in sleep in which is given rest from labors I had respite and it was evidently from Satan and (it) was pursuing. And I hoped that you would cheer up my hope and console me but you frightened me with visions.

And you have examined my soul, more than those (plagues) with which I am tortured your words and your dreams torment me. I am sick, i.e., of your words and why do you worry me and condemn me with your words?

And he says to God: What is man that you should destroy him? And that you should inspect (him) in the morning
and examine him in the evening? i.e., with your clear judgment you examine him and kill him now (lit. today) and you have put upon your heart to inspect him in the morning of resurrection and you scrutinize him in an excellent manner in the judgment.

And till when will you not forgive me, (who am in such a position) that here is death and trials and there judgment and anguish. Will you not turn away from me until I shall swallow down my spittle? If I have sinned what shall I do to thee? i.e., you should lay off on me (lit. may any soul be bored for you from me) you set free, you forgive, you repeat your gifts; you have made me that I may know you from your ways: Let me meet you in your judgment when I shall see you in person and stand before you.

And now I have become a burden to myself, i.e., I have become spoil. You have visited me with trials you have subdued me with needs and when will you forgive my crime and forgot my follies lest (lit. so that) it shall come to pass: Lo, I am lying down and you seek me but I shall not be (lit. It may have come to pass indicating direct speech; and perfect to be taken as perfect future).
And Bildad answered and said: How long wilt thou speak, a haughty spirit being in thine mouth, i.e. because he said: And you have destined me to meet you.

Does God pervert judgment? i.e., he teaches that Job was punished justly because of his sins and the sins of his children inasmuch as God does not judge falsely. Ask of God, i.e., he also teaches this that if it be that a man has sinned there should be prayer and expiation for him, then his latter will be better than his former.
I am enquiring about the former age, i.e., I have observed that nobody admonishes or teaches that man is punished without having sinned.

Is the swamp abundant in a place, i.e., to the swamp and the reed he likens God's afflictions and he says that they are not where there are no sins. And if it be that the reeds, as we have heard are cut after that they have thrown their fruit, then allow the death of those you loved to become occasion to that you heal your soul (lit.: Heal your soul by the death of your beloved ones, i.e., let the punishment bear fruit so that it can be removed like the reeds).

It is as moisture before the sun, i.e., the house of the wicked before the burning righteousness of God. And upon stalks his roots, i.e., he likens the wicked to stalks and grass which quickly pass away and are singed. And he sees the house of stone, i.e., in his humiliation. And if he roots him out from his place, i.e., from this world. And he will deceive him, i.e., God, (lit. he will deceive God) in this world, and he will say: I have not seen him, and:
I have not broken your commandments and your laws. Lo he examines all his ways, i.e., Because follies and sins are not hidden from him. And from the dust another shall grow, i.e., When he is resurrected from the dust a different one will be found, i.e., a humile one instead of a hard one and a supplicant one instead of a ferocious one and a good one instead of an evil one.

God does not cast away the perfect ones, i.e., If you have been perfect and not committed evil these things are in store for you. Job says: One thousand-part he could not answer him, i.e., If God would dispute with him he could not answer to one thousand-part of the reproaches (with) which he (God) would reproach, i.e., Not even for one thousand-part of the follies (which he commits) there is excuse to man.

He who commanded the sun and it did not rise. i.e., In Egypt, three days--while the sun was moving above the earth--it looked to the Egyptians as if it did not rise. (Exod. X. 21 ff. Compare Bar Salibi on this passage) And sealeth up the stars, i.e., With dark clouds. And passes over the bottom of the sea, i.e., When he divided it before the Hebrews passing over in front.

If he passes me I do not see him, i.e., By reason of his hiddenness and infinite nature. God does not turn back his wrath, i.e., Nobody can resist him, repentance however makes this (i.e. the wrath) turn back.

Many helpers are humiliated. i.e., The heroes of men and demons are trodden under him. And I shall not believe until he has heard my voice, i.e., I shall not abstain from asking until I am answered. If I should be victorious my own mouth would subjugate me, i.e., If I should gain the point that I possess righteous manners my mouth should subjugate me by (uttering) haughty words.

I am perfect and I do not know, i.e., I am perfect according to myself but I do not know how I am estimated according to him. My soul despises my life, i.e., When I am victorious (or pure) in it (i.e., in my life) I have no pleasure and when I am perfect I am destroyed with anguish and I do not know if my perfectness is (reckoned as) perversity, i.e., perversity according to him.

It is one, I think that all men are in wrong before him. He lets the righteous and the wicked perish, i.e., In tribulation and judgment. And he laughs from contempt of the innocent, i.e., Because he has no need of the innocence of the innocent ones but they, and although they are innocent his rod may kill them suddenly in which case their innocence is of no use to them.

He gives the earth, i.e., His body. In the hands of the wicked one, i.e., Satan. He covers up the faces of the judges, i.e., Of my friends who vituperate me. My days are swifter than runners, i.e., (from) when a runner starts to run until he rests from his running thus are my days swift and they go in pain and they do not see good (things)

With my pain I have forgotten what I used to care for, i.e., By reason of pains of my soul I have desisted from seeking answers (to problems) and (from) contemplating over justice which used to be useful to me. If I abandon my worries and if I comfort myself a little I am afraid, i.e., If I despise your punishment I would be like him who does not take into account the one who whips him.

If I be guilty, i.e., I shall become weak in judgment or (I am guilty) by reason of sins. And if I wash myself with waters, i.e., With penitence and tears of righteousness until I shall say that crime is not on my hands. Then you plunge me in the ditch, i.e., Because I have become haughty from righteousness. My clothes will be far from me, i.e., Excellencies and the body. Oh that there were a daysman between us, i.e., A mediator who could clear up the truth. And I will speak in bitterness of my soul, i.e., It cannot be blamed that I speak of (?) my trials.

And I shall say to God: Do not condemn me, i.e., For that which I am asking. Show me wherefore thou contendest with me, i.e., Because of which folly I am punished for because Job did not know--because Satan (and not any sin of his which he might have known) was the urger of his affliction--he said: Show me that because of which I am worthy of afflictions. It is not right for you that you have harmed me, i.e., Because you have wrecked a vessel which you had formed which was without faults. And you have looked at the opinion of the
wicked, i.e., You neglected their wickedness and you look benevolent from with the insolent. Are your eyes as the eyes of flesh, i.e., In this he exalts him above (the ide) that he should be alike to man in nature because the creator is exalted over the creation. And he says that as you are not alike to your work thus it is not right for you to neglect it when it is pursued without guilt. You enquire about my iniquities and my sins, i.e., You find in me iniquities and sins.

Although you know (text: and I know) that I am innocent, i.e., In quarreling with an tormenting an innocent you persist in that I must have sinned or do you usually judge the righteous ones and the wicked ones (for) something which does not exist?

Your hands have laboured with me and fashioned me, i.e., By this he reminds him: even if I have no deeds by reason of which I can be saved, your being creator should remind you for you created me in grace, and now you destroy me in wrath; this be far from you. And you cause me to return to the dust, i.e., Independent of Moses he teaches on the forming of Adam and the verdict which was (pronounced) against him.

And my soul has kept thy commandments, i.e., I have not been idle since (lit. from) you created me. If I have sinned you will guard me, i.e., Because verily I know that
you do not decide in favor of those who sin. And if the decision be in my favor I shall not lift up my head, i.e., I shall not become haughty because of my righteousness because this is not what I like (lit. this is not dear unto me) but what I shall do I do not know, sins cause woe and righteousness affliction.

And again you would display your valiance upon me, i.e., When it was thus fixed that I should become your enemy, why (then) have you created me? Then I had been through and eyes had not seen me, i.e., Oh that I had not come into existence so that you had not punished me and eyes had not seen me that I should become an irritation to you. And they had carried me from the womb to the grave, i.e., It would have been best that I had died and when my existence had been like non-existence then you would not have become enraged.

That I might rest a little, i.e., From the punishment and the trial. To the land of darkness (lit. to the dark land) i.e., To the grave. Not are in it series of generations, i.e., Conception and birthgiving and generation after generation.

He said of: Sophar the Na'amatite. Lo the dead ones may be silent to your words. Those who do not feel may stand the acuteness (the edge M.S.: the deletion) of your words, I however am alive (and) I will not be silent.

You talk and nobody restrains thee, i.e., You believe that we have no words which would understand you (i.e., find you out) and punish you. And if thou mockest shall no man make thee ashamed? i.e., Do you think that we have as much intelligence as you, that we understand what you say and can answer thee? --and this is because he(Job) would have them believe that he was punished unjustly in as much as he was innocent. (lit. because of his innocence.)

But O that, etc. That God's hidden mysteries might be revealed to you and the wide range (lit. limit) of his justice which are unknown to you. Wisdom has an inner side, i.e., An infinite mysterium. And if these were revealed you would know that God has (even) made the allowance for your sins.

Are you able to understand (the task of) exploring God? i.e., By this he teaches that God cannot be understood nor can his creation be measured. Man cannot comprehend the ends of heaven nor examine the depth of Sheol. If he will pass, fetch and gather, who can answer it? In another way If he passes and fetches and gathers all the Gentiles to his judgment who not even any among the angels, i.e., The time and hour on which the judgment will be and the dead will rise, this judgment cannot be known (lit. sensed) because no one knows the depth of wisdom. Because he knows when the time will be, i.e., Of the resurrection and judgment. And the
crook sees... i.e., He does not care that there will be to him claim and judgment, when he passes by, fetches and gathers all tribes. And nobody can turn him back, i.e., He that created worlds in grace and judges everybody according to his deeds and righteous men are cheered up by him those who are prevalent in strength, and they help them in repentance--for this shows that: and who is a hero helps men--there and here in the time of trial so that they are cheered up.

And if you had directed (right) your heart, i.e., If you had been thus you would not have been castigated with trials. And if there were iniquity, i.e., If you had been a crook he would forgive you because of penitence and prayer on your part. And you did not let iniquity dwell in your tent, i.e., When there was not iniquity in you then you lifted your hands in trust and from torment you did not fear, i.e., from death.

And like passing waters you will do, i.e., Those which the clouds carry on their wings and elevate to heaven, thus also you will be lifted from the plagues, and what was yours will be given back to you. And from midday he will rise (from?) the pit, i.e., He calls the trial a pit and good works midday like this He made and sent out like the day your righteousness. Further from midday i.e., from (i.e., out of) patience and good deeds and not uttering blasphemy rises for him the pit, i.e., the making ashamed of the Accuser. And darkness like morning, i.e., The trials and the castigations which surround you become light before you
so as to be (wholly) forgotten by (reason of) the righteousness and purity and your darkness is turned into light, and your pain into gladness. And you can trust that there is hope for your future, i.e., When those things come to you then you can trust (i.e., then you have proof) that there is a redeemer who erects and rescues.

And you will sleep and rest, i.e., There shall not be any who scared you up nor shall trials afflict you, because of which you are (now) crying, and all fear of strife shall be far away from thee like from one asleep. And many shall seek your face, i.e., The peoples of the earth who existed (at that time) and those who were about to come shall seek you and they be eager to see your face.

And the eyes of the wicked ones are darkened, i.e., The eyes of the Accuser and the demons are darkened by your innocence. And the hope of their souls, i.e., Their hopes have ceased, i.e., that by such things you might sin, and remove you from God. Job answered and said:

Verily you are the people, i.e., Who understand and know. And with you wisdom dies, i.e., Because there is none so wise as you. Also I have a heart, i.e., An intelligent one. To whom happened like these? i.e., That he was tried in trials like I And cried it out to God and he answered him, i.e., I have cried to him in those trials that he should remember me lest I should act wickedly and commit blasphemy and he has answered me; for I know that God is not in the heart of those who plunder and rage against God.

Ask the animals and they will answer thee, i. e.,
He teaches that from all creatures (as a whole) as well as from each of them, from it and because of it we learn that there is a creator like this: The heaven shall tell the glory of God.

Because of his hands, i.e., The souls and spirits, everything sensible and intelligent exists by his hands for he (is the one who) made and created. Accordingly these things did not happen to me independently of him. The ear hears words and the palate tastes food, i.e., You have fame and wisdom and intelligence and they ought to be salted in truth lest when you were short of taste and kindness and intelligence you should also be without discernment for if it be that (of) the palate and the ear this descerns, this understands then it is seeming that also the intelligence be thus in order that it may understand and discern that wisdom is of God -- and he rules all and that from him are those things which are heavy on me (lit. which I carry).

If he rebukes the waters they dry up, i.e., Like what happened in the time of Moses in the Red Sea and in the days of Joshua bar Nun in Jordan. And he lets them loose, Like the typhoon in the days of Noah. He leads kings, i.e., By these things he teaches (about) the kingdom of God and his administration (lit. cares) that the kings and priests who were in the days of Job should wonder at them. He leads the priests by means of wondering, i.e., That they should wonder at his miracles without scrutinizing his greatness.

And he lowereth the strong ones, i.e., Like those who were in the days of Israel from the beginning until the rise of Christ. He causes the word to pass from the believers, i.e., By those (words) he teaches that those who have come to know God also have sought to propagate. To those all of it fits. It is (however) also conceived of (as) referring to the demons. Further it is conceived of as relating to the descent of the Lord to the earth and Sheol and the stopping of the power of the demons.

I however will speak to the powerful one, i.e., Because I know, that he hears me I am speaking the truth, and you have no words of healing. Hear my blame, i.e., He blames them because they have charged him falsely in that they believe that he is castigated because he has sinned. Further, even granted that he had sinned, did they come to his pain to console him or to do him harm?

You talk iniquity of God, i.e., Of God they spoke and pretended that they had knowledge while they did not (even) know the will of Job. Would you like him to scrutinise you? i.e., Is it worse that he should examine you (now) as he has examined me, than that he should do harm (to) you for my sake as it happened in the end? Why must I carry my flesh with my teeth? i.e., It has reference to the hardness of the pain: that if I could eat my flesh with my teeth until I was consumed perhaps I might rest. My soul is placed in my hands, i.e., Because there was not an intact body (in which it could be). If he will kill me I am waiting (eagerly) for him, i.e.,
He praises his slayer who knows that if he kills him he gives him life for he knows that he is just and merciful; and I trust him like this: When I am weak I am strong. (Comp. II Cor. 12-10)

My ways are before him, i.e., My alms, my purity. Change does not enter before him, i.e., He does not change so as to return evil for good. I know that I am innocent, i.e., Which witness stood up against me now and accused me before you so that I had to keep quiet and could not speak?

Only two things you must not cause to pass from me, i.e., Not the benefactions of this world nor those of the coming one. In another way that if the temporal benefits you have caused to pass away from me, those of the coming world you must not cause to pass and from before thee in the other world and the redeemer do not throw me (away), when you open up your gate remember me and do not part from me in your resurrection.

Thy fear may not frighten me, i.e., Your judgment. And call me and I shall answer, i.e., From Sheol, from the grave, for (in a manner that will take me) out of the judgment I shall plead (my case) when you ask (me) in the judgment. Or I shall speak and do you answer me! How many are my crimes and sins? i.e., How many are my crimes and sins that you repudiate me from mercy here and yonder and how can my sins be more numerous than your mercy? And you have considered me an enemy, How can you now consider me an enemy when you created me in mercy, and oppress me and contend (with me)?

A withered torn off leaf which fell down you trample under foot, Being God your existence is one of spirit and I am material and a servant, how can I stand before thee and be victorious? as also the leaf cannot stand before him who tramples it. You have put my feet in fetters, i.e., In pains and vexations. And you have watched all my ways, i.e., As if I were able to flee from before thee. And he is like a cloth that is rotten. And you look at the strength of my feet, i.e., As if I were able to go ahead of thee (only) a little and go and hide myself from you, you have put me in fetters that I shall not flee.

And he likens lateron man to herbs and grass and (says) that God tolerates him because of his (Gods) grace and he says to him: Also upon him are your eyes opened and you enter him to judgment. Oh that a pure (might come) from an impure! not even one! It is not within the boundaries of man, and not one is innocent that he can go out to judgment with God. And as you do not find an innocent between guilty ones thus also there is not any among men who is victorious in the judgment and when you declare them innocent the victory is yours.

If his days are fixed, i.e., Short and confided (to him) only in measure. You have made a law, i.e., You have established a law namely a boundary which nobody can transgress because nobody lives eternally.

His days are like those of a hireling, i.e., Because the days of labor in this world are going to be completed.
Further: Which nobody transgresses, i.e., Leave him that he may run like a hireling until the completion of his time and when his labor is completed then he is rewarded his hire.

Because there is hope for the wood, i.e., The wood, physical human hope. i.e., This he says, that based on the wood, which has been cut off there is hope for men; that he will grow and (then) grow a second time. He is cut off, i.e., in death, further he grows a second time in resurrection when he arises. Further, (even) if the wood feels that it is cut off its hope is not cut off as it (the wood) grows again how much more than men when he is redeemed according to his deeds by God to immortality and Christ turns him into infragility.

And its sprigs do not cease, i.e., Because the soul is alive. Even if the body waits for a time to be released, still it is preserved intact in the earth. And its sprigs, i.e., That even if a liar (text: nature) is cut off because of evilness the true and righteous ones are not cut off because of goodness. Further And its sprigs, i.e., He comes back and rises and acquires wealth like before.

And if its root grows old in the earth, i.e., If he stays a long time in the earth, yet he is known to God because he is going to raise him up. Further And if it grows old in the earth because of very long time, and dies in the dust, i.e., Because it is not inundated.

From the wind of waters, i.e., Before those of Baptism and teaching in which the human nature is united with Christ. Further From wind i.e., And running waters of that well of life, Christ, who raises the dead ones. Further: after that it has received inundation of the water its leaves and its sprigs bloom like a tree which is planted anew. And it produces leaves, i.e., Of faith and knowledge of Christ; in his likeness it is planted in Paradise. Further: Leaves are the immortality and infragility in which he is clothed in the resurrection.

Further: If accordingly there is hope for the wood that when it has been cut off it may grow again (then the fact) that man dies and putrefies will not destroy his wages so that he is not resurrected. A man who dies and putrefies, i.e., In effect and by the looks of it this is so, however the following does not permit (the explanation) that he (Job) should have thought that he was not going to rise again, and that he should bear witness (to that effect) (i.e., that he was not going to rise).

Further: dead i.e., The man who is dead his life is cut off and he has killed (sic!) and does not exist from then off. The waters cease, i.e., By this he demonstrates that everything is stopped and is dissolved. Further: The waters cease from the sea, i.e., The waters of the sea namely, are sometimes few and then they again return to their former state. And rivers dry up and become dry.

And a man who lies down, i.e., A man who dies does not rise and come back to this life. Further: A man who lies down does not rise, i.e., Any man lies down and dies alone but he cannot rise alone but he rises together with those who are awakened and praise. When the heaven perish; for when the heavens have perished they (the dead) shiver and are awakened from their sleep and that it is thus testified this which he says:

Oh that you would forget me in Sheol, i.e., I wished that I would not rise but would be forgotten in Sheol, otherwise I would have to stand before you when you judge me. That you would hide me until the wrath had passed, i.e., Your judgment. And that you would establish a treaty with me and remember me, i.e., That you would resurrect me to deliver me so that you would not do me any harm, and this is said in the manner of a pauper from his fear of the judgment. If a man dies, i.e., Because after death there is no return to this world. And all the days of his youth he waits until comes his old age, i.e., Because he knows that in the time of old age he receives rest from toil he knows that there is no escape from (lit. scheme against) death and he awaits it. And therefore he is in fear and his life is bitter from fear of death.

And If you call me I shall answer thee, i.e., Because I know that I am awake in the waiting for you and my soul looks for you and is not asleep from seeking you and therefore I expect that you will call me. The work of your hands is thought of, i.e., I am guarded under your hand and your hand
takes care of me. Because do you not now count my steps? i.e., I am dying and my steps decrease (in number). And will you not guard my sins, i.e., Hide my iniquities under a seal so that they are not seen before you.

Certainly a strong mountain, Like I have fallen because of your vituperation and I am not a mountain but a withered leaf, torn off by your strength. Does a rock wound waters? i.e., And like these things are not found to exist thus even if my hope perishes now in the affliction yet you are going to strengthen me forever.

In shame of his face you throw him, i.e., (only) to become a mockery for my friends he has let me loose from trial to a place of mirth.Further, that if you destroy his hope he goes in shame of his face and you deject him from before thee. And if his sons are many he does not know, i.e., Not whether they are many and not whether they are few or whether he has not any. But he is in pain on account of his hope, i.e., He who is in bodily pain and whose soul is depressed from the divine punishments has no delight in children nor in wealth because he knows that he is rejected by God. Further: The hope of man, i.e., Because he believes that he may rise by his own power; for you are the one who strengthens him forever.

div.head: The speech of Elifas.
div.ab:
A wise of heart answers with knowledge, i.e., He admonishes and corrects. And anger fills his stomach, i.e., In the sense of zeal. Also you make fear (of God) cease, i.e., You are strong in your trial and make fear of God cease
and speak before him without fear and you are haughty from righteousness and therefore as much as is in your mouth is sins, and while well-deserved punishments are seen on you you consider yourself to be right.

Were you perhaps borne as the first man? i.e., Perhaps you were the first man who entered the world since you speak as if you were the only one on earth and (as if) there were not any to reproach you, and we are reckoned as animals before you. Keep away from you the menaces of God, i.e., Because according to that your words are strong thus your punishment is much. And speak easy to yourself, i.e., With yourself. Why is your heart haughty? i.e., Since you say that you have been treated unjustly by the creator. And you raise up toward God . . . i.e., You equal yourself to God although you are a human and of human nature.

Not can a woman-borne be considered just. Lo, in his holy ones he does not trust, there is none like him, nor his equal among the holy ones of heaven and earth. And the heavens are not pure, i.e., The angels are not pure before him as his equal as to purity does not exist. Even if man is rejected and torn off, i.e., In temptations. What wise ones have demonstrated and not hid (which they received) from their fathers, i.e., He accepts the teaching from those.

To those only the earth was given, i.e., Because of their righteousness from the time of the house of Noah. And no foreigner had passed between them, i.e., In the freighter, the Ark, from one side to the other not even one
of the wicked ones were saved. . . . . of the wicked one he exalts himself, i.e., In his wicked desire and he does not turn back. And the number of his years is watched by the powerful one, i.e., By him who is careful in the judgment that he repays wickedness. A voice of horror in his ears, i.e., From nearby comes to him the horror of judgment and he cannot flee.

In peace a robber comes, i.e., When he hopes that he is in peace and safety trial comes over him, i.e., the lethal day of judgment. He does not believe that he must turn away from the darkness, i.e., He does not expect that his dark deeds are made public but he expects to go on forward in his iniquities. He sees the sword and flees from the menace of the judgment, i.e., If he hides himself beneath the hand of God when he is going to be repaid from it (he may possibly flee from the judgment).

The day of darkness, i.e., It is the judgment. As a king who prepares to fight, i.e., The day of judgment comes against him with all punishment and torments. Because he lifted his hand, i.e., Even Israel rebelled against him in the end, against the son of God and hardened its neck against the Lord. And he covered his face with his fat, i.e., His face was covered with lust like this: Israel grew fat and kicked, (Deut. 32.15) i.e., like this In his hardness he removed shame from his face and he had proclaimed that also the works of God he would change if he could, i.e., bring to pass. He made a swelling above the pleiades (?) i.e.,
A covering of fat, a swelling above his flancs. And he caused desolate villages to be inhabited, i.e., His enterprises which were physically strong by wealth (used) contrary to (the will) of its giver, i.e., they were bad all of them; or Jericho whose ruins were cursed not to be inhabited. Also idols which were desolate (may be meant) and with this he prepares to the fight against God.

And therefore his army will not prevail and not rise, i.e., His synagogue will be scattered and his kingdom devastated. He shall not throw words on earth, i.e., He shall not give commands and not give judgment on earth. He shall not quit darkness, i.e., That which consists of shame and of sin. The flame shall dry up . . i.e., The heat of punishments. He shall act foolishly with the breath (of his mouth) i.e., Through those (two things) that he says and believes that he is a believer.

He would not believe in seductive lies, i.e., He should not believe in seducive wealth and lie, which stays with him. Vain was his scion, i.e., In vain they were planted and they vanished from the place. And not in his season he withered, i.e., Because of his iniquity and not because of any wish of God's. And his hand could not, i.e., He had no strength so that he could help himself. He will root out like a vine his flesh, i.e., His children who were
carnal like himself. And he will throw like the olive-tree his scion, i.e., He will be beaten with staffs which are punishments and this (means): because he became a pagan he was destroyed, and the fire of wrath consumed them because they conceived iniquity and gave birth to fraud. Job said: You console me as profligate ones all of you, He refers to his friends that they are profligate, because while they came to console him they repeated to him what God does of acts of revenge against crooks which added pain upon pain upon him; and therefore he rebukes them.

He has made me tired, i.e., God, with the trials which I suffer (lit. have). And he rose me up and I became a witness, i.e., Those things which have been done unto me of trials bear witness according to the look of them that because I have acted wickedly I am repaid. My lie arose against me, i.e., Although he knows that he is not false, yet because he speaks with God he is considered by him(self) mendacious in comparison with God's unspeakable truth.

The earth shall not cover my blood, i.e., When it cries against Satan like that of Abel. Not be there a place for my cries, i.e., Something that will hold back my cry. From (the idea) that God might not hear my groans.

Now, lo! in heaven are my witnesses, i.e., Good deeds and treasures consisting in alms which I have deposed in heaven according to: Make yourself deposits in heaven (Mat. 6.20, Luke 12.33) i.e., with God who is hidden in hiddenness as if in heaven.

A certain man further says that the souls of the just and righteous which he had delivered and satiated testify to his righteousness. And a number of his years are coming, i.e., When he dies it will be known how much he has lived. Because there is no lie in me, i.e., Therefore Satan and the demons smote me and had no mercy upon me because they did not find in me lie. And in their bitterness my soul did not pass the night, i.e., The bitternesses of the whips of the demons.

Establish please my tent with you, i.e., He says to God: Now you have destroyed my tent on earth, establish then (?) a house and dwelling place for me in heaven, i.e., build for me a house with you in heaven. He knew that God is good and therefore he asks that he is remunerated in heaven.

They have stolen those things which were mine, i.e., My wealth. Who is the one, i.e., Who endured like I (have done). But are not my friends wise that they rebuke: Therefore he will not exalt them, i.e., God. They (Fem.) will grow dark, i.e., They are dark. You have made me a famous one among the nations, i.e., Because nobody was tried and endured like me. I have become a mockery, i.e., For the demons.
They are dim, i.e., The eyes of the heart which those trials of which I do not know the cause, have blurred. I am a captive etc., i.e., Because everybody believes that this is a revenge for sins.

But wondering etc., i.e., The angels or the righteous ones the just one, however, who is tried, i.e., Job. To the believing one, i.e., This is Job. You resist, i.e., You doubt that this is a trial and not a punishment. However, lo, all of you, i.e., Who were with you in the resistance. Are divided, i.e., Your thoughts are seperated from your words. They make night to day, i.e., Of him who is tempted because of righteousness you say that this has happened to him because of iniquity.

For if I endure, i.e., Your words, that I do not answer I am captivated in vexation like in Sheol. In darkness, i.e., of trials. I have cried: Father, i.e., Because of the hardness of the trials he longs for the end and seeks it; and the one who hopes for those things, which hope is left for him except that of resurrection? And that one had not yet been revealed. Or do I see my blessings? i.e., Lo, I have been deprived of all of them. Bildad the Shuhite answered him--

--How long will he keep on with words about (the fact) that man is erring most of which aim to rebuke Job? - words, among which are descriptions of the curses and the revenge which reaches the wicked because of their unlawfulness and which--according to Bildad--are seen in effect on Job; for even if this abominable curse and revenge has reference to the wicked, yet the reproof hits Job because plenty of this kind was seen upon him. (Lit. Until when will he not rest from words that man is erring, the multitude of which rebukes
Job, and among them are curses and revenge which reaches the wicked ones because of their unlawfulness, which (the curses) according to Bildad can be seen in effect upon Job. And even if this abominable curse and revenge has reference to the wicked ones yet because plenty of this was seen on Job, therefore the reproof hits him). Job answers--not to their reproof however, which he skips--and asks, saying:

Have mercy on me, have mercy on me, namely that they shall show mercy on him and not weary him and excite him to wrath with rebuking words and he adds that: he hopes that his words may be written down; i.e., Because he knew that he was not punished because of his sins as his friends thought for he was certain that he was tried a trial, and therefore he asked that his words were written down because he knew that after a little while the former state would return to him, for he relied upon hope because he knew that God is good and just and in as much as he was not guilty of those things which the friends said that he had committed or thought; and therefore he wished that what he had said was written down so that when he went out from the trial the friends might remember his words and see that he was right and they wrong.

And that you may know the truth ofthis, lo! he adds and says: For I know that he is without end, i.e., God who is infinite and whose decisions cannot be understood and the depths of whose guidance cannot be known. He will let me dwell on earth, that he may give back to me my former (state). And he raises up my skin, i.e., The body which suffered all
those afflictions giving it rest from toils and pains and trials. If, however, a man should like to take those words as referring to the later resurrection he will not err from the truth.

Those are from the Lord to me, i.e., I know that the Lord has tried me and I have been enthrusted with (the ability) that I can see with spiritual (lit. allegorical) eyes that this is a trial and not a retaliation, and all of them (i.e., the trials) I know to be perfecting me in the bosom, for the trial through temptation is in reality the perfection of the righteous in excellency and love of God; that which exalts toward perfection and causes to attain the divine breasts which our Lord calls the bosom of Abraham.

If, however, you say: What shall we say before him? i.e., Because you do not know that the hiddenness of the reason for my punishment you judge from what is seen (i.e., from external matters only). And you do not know what you say. Be terrified from the hidden! i.e., Fear what is hidden; and you should not judge it when you do not know its cause lest perhaps it should not be as you think and figure.

The answer of Sophar in which he disclosed the retaliation which is to the wicked in this world shooting his words against Job (like arrows) and reproaching him: And therefore these things came over you because of your wickedness. And in the beginning of his speech he says that he hoped that he would answer back etc. i.e., I have not become convinced that God has permitted those things which are seen
upon you to be upon you, not because you have deserved them but as a temptation. You can however take also the rest of his words on the wicked as referring to the later judgment and the ending of iniquity in general and the depriving of the sweetness of the kingdom. That you may comprehend however that the speech of Sophar is about the retaliation of the wicked ones Behold! Job answers him and says:

Hear my words, i.e., In these (i.e., the words) Job demonstrates: lo, the wicked were numerous in the world and not happened unto them anything like what you have mentioned but they died rich. According to what you have told--and also the Psalmist has written this--what is the reason that on me alone is seen that God took revenge but let the others alone? Consequently when this is thus, there (must) be something which is hidden from you (and) which you do not know.

And he curses later on the wicked ones, asking that they be retaliated, but even if they die in this world while they are rich it (the retaliation) is preserved for them. And by reason of this man understands that a multitude of wicked ones can be in this world from whom revenge is not taken, thus there are also many righteous ones who are tormented in this life while their remuneration is preserved for the next life. And if this were not so it would be right that the righteous and also the wicked ones were retaliated here. And (it speaks) further for the truth of these things which have been said that thus it (actually) is (in the world).

Job added and said: Another dies from bitterness of soul etc. In the Peshitta: This dies with a soul of bitterness when he eats and nothing (tastes) good. Together they lie down against the door, i.e., The righteous and the wicked by reason of death. And he reproves them because of their mercy toward him (which was of this nature) that they said to him that he was punished because of his wickedness. And he teaches them that they shall ask concerning those who go by the way. And their forebodes (signs) you do not understand, i.e., The just and righteous ones which were the world, further the prophets who were to rise were harrassed in this world which he calls the way, for the sake of the life and remuneration in the coming world and like (it is with) them (it is) also (with) the wicked ones, that they are not retaliated; and from this which is seen in the world, i.e., the harrassing of the righteous and the wicked not being retaliated learn (lit. understand) that not in this world is the judgment but that the retaliation of those is kept for the coming judgment, that which he calls: the day of utterly destruction and disaster and wrath. Concerning that they are not retaliated here, concerning that the wicked ones and the righteous ones enter the grave both of them, yet those are kept for adversity, which the Syriac (version) calls accident, and these for soft days.

But I shall now inquire concerning this, which is seen in the world, also the Prophets and their writings and the Evangel and from them I shall teach the truth concerning those things which are seen in the world, and from these (the Prophets) and this (the Evangel) I am convinced that this world is a road which leads to another place, the one in which is retaliation, because this world is one of toil and also of trials by means of labour and it is befitting that another one of retaliation should rise as teach the words of Job and of the Prophets and of the New Testament.

After these matters Elifas blames him openly: Not are these matters a trial as you think but a retaliation for sins, and an admonishing to him that if he repents he will be accepted. And later on Job answers out of his knowledge that he is innocent and he expects that if God would speak with him or dispute (with him) he could answer him and if he (Job) saw him or came to him perhaps he (Job) would be victorious and the wrath would be lifted from him but it is not possible to get in contact with God and he cannot be seen; he says, however, that he knows that he has kept his laws and I have not committed iniquity but I cannot contend against him because his decisions are too high for me.

He says, however: A multitude of misdeeders have not been retaliated by him in this world; why then I, who have not committed iniquity? And while he relates those things which the wicked ones do he curses them. Bildad answers him and says that no creature can stand against God because of his
strength. How then can you say: (If) I could speak with him I would be victorious. Job answers and relates the glorious deeds of God and he demonstrates that he knows him better than Bildad. However, he, who is that strong and mighty is just and not one evil word is accepted by him but he judges justly.

Further: Whom do you condemn? this he says to Bildad. He whose strength is plenty, i.e., God. Whom have you advised? i.e., Nor are you able to advise God and not to become like God but you follow God. Because to whom have you shown the strength of his power? i.e., And nobody has learned from you and how can you wish to be a teacher to me if I know that the matters of God are greater than those you have mentioned. Are perhaps counsellors borne under the waters and from their (aquatic) plants?

Sheol is laid bare, i.e., So that the souls can be brought (there). To us they are invisible but to him they are revealed. And there is not a cover for the annihilation, i.e., And the (component) parts of those bodies which you think perish and are dissolved (text promise) are laid bare to him, i.e., (even) when they are mixed with the dust. Who extended the north upon nothing, i.e., By the one region which he mentions out of the four regions he indicates that also the others and the firmament and the earth and the world
which is in the middle are hanging upon nothing.
