He hang up the earth upon nothing, i.e., By his command and by his power--from the beginning and till the end--the earth hangs in the air and in the fire and in the heaven which surrounds it, for there is not vacuity between those but they rest upon nothing, not supporting each other, for the air does not support the earth nor the fire the air nor the heavens all of them.

He bound the waters in the clouds, i.e., When the clouds carry the waters--and it is in the nature of the waters that they go down, i.e., although it is natural for water to fall down, yet, etc.--they do not lacerate them (i.e., the clouds) and go down but by reason of the command they behave in a floating fashion and quietly one after another they come down and there is nothing which supports the clouds and the waters in them. He who is substituted by the throne(i.e., for whom the throne is a substitute) i.e., In the place of (i.e., where he says:) that which our Lord calls heaven and commands that a person shall not swear by heaven because it is the throne of God, it (the firmament or throne) is, however, an aphorismus which stands for God by (reason of) this this, that while it is placed on nothing, he causes it skillfully to turn around the center and the place is not changed from the movement with which it is moved, not to the right and not to the left and not up and not down. In another way: A substitute for heaven, i.e., Because he does not permit that it is lacerated or that that which is above it is revealed.

Further: A substitute for it because he moves it and it is not moved by (its own) nature. He stretches out his clouds over it, i.e., Now and then he hides it in clouds because of the abundance which comes from them. A commandment he let circle the face of the waters, i.e., On the two limits of the sea, that which is with us and that which is outside the other ends of the earth, he placed a limit lest they (the waters) should pass over and cover the earth or incline from this side and perish. And this that he let surround teaches that the sea is circular and surrounds the dry land like a ring.

The columns of heaven flew and were astonished at his vituperation, i.e., He refers to the angels who are in heaven and he calls them columns because they are of firm nature and immortal. And they are flying constantly on the allegorical wings of the mind, those with which they are longing for God. They are astonished (i.e., admire) however at the vituperation of God when he rebukes the Accuser and the demons and repels and throws them.

Further: The columns of heaven, he calls the sun and the moon and the stars which flew from the elements and ascended on the first day and mixed themselves with the original light and on the fourth day they were separated from each other and planted upon the firmament and stood (there) and now they are pillars which do not cease moving (lit.: separate themselves from constant movement.) They are astounded, however, at his vituperation, i.e., It is the habit of the scripture that it
ascribes vituperation and wondering also to the inanimate nature like this that he rebuked the sea and dried it up and he dries up the rivers and he rebuked the mountains and they repeated. Accordingly reproof and wondering befall the inanimate from God when he suspends their nature that which was done unto the sun and the moon in the time of Josua bar Nun and Hezekiah and in (this) connection: it is also going to be seen in the end when the sun and the moon darken and the stars fall.

In his strength he rebukes the sea, i.e., Lest it shall become haughty by reason of its waves and immerse the earth. By his knowledge the whale planes out, i.e., The Tannina which is in the sea that is plane and lies in its place; and when it (the whale) moves in the full magnitude of its nature it does not disturb the sea and does not (cause it) to overflow and does not move (it).

The bonds of heaven fear him, i.e., If he shuts like in the days of Elijah who can open? and if he opens like in the days of Noah who can shut? and who is able to enter and lacerate the firmament or to cut away from it? By his command he kills the rebellious serpent, i.e., That sensible and crafty one which made Adam err and killed him in sin. Lo, those are part of his way, i.e., His deeds are of his wonders which are in the world. And further, A drop of his word do we hear, i.e., Other works and deeds of his word
are going to be heard and seen from his wisdom and his word and these became reality when the word became flesh and descended as a drop upon the mown grass and the righteous bloomed in his days.

Who knows the strength of his thunder, i.e., When he shall act, i.e., Although these are obscure matters and a token: when the apparatus of thunder mingles with the clouds; yet because it is said prophetically and like in allegory (it refers) to the thunder of the Evangel and the powerful revealing of the good message.

And Job continues and says with oaths that he has not committed sin nor does (he at present) and that the perfectness which he has kept he keeps and holds firmly (The text originally read: Which he has kept and keeps he holds firmly) and he curses the words of his enemies and demonstrates later on that the Lord does not answer the wicked in affliction and how can he be a wicked and rejected who demonstrates that which God intends to do to the wicked ones and who know and understands it. And he praises that God thus retaliates those who sin against him and act wickedly and that he lets the righteous inherit their possessions according to the opinion which was once held.

And he continues that there is a place for the silver and for the gold etc. from which they come and by this he teaches that even if God is the cause of these (things) also man knows, and understands, and knows the exhumation of such things, i.e., (knows) the place of silver, brass, and iron
and it is right that they (men) should know also the creator of these things and not act wickedly. He has established order for the darkness, that as long as it lasts, at the failing of the light, he (man) lets the toil rest and for a time he is unoccupied and it were right that even from this he (God) should be known.

And he knows all perfection, i.e., Even if he knows all, if (he knows) not the evil desire and the Accuser, him whom he calls the stone of darkness and the shadow of death, the evil will issue forth and a river not to be crossed will come from it by the intervention of earthly desires, those which he calls dust, all of which exist that they (men) may be deverted by them from the way of righteousness and are ruined from being good men; and while the earth is common (to all) and the cause of all good things and they know it and act skilfully, yet they do not conclude from it to its creator.

Under it like fire is turned, i.e., Under the earth, i.e., In the midst of it things are turned by means of a whirlpool into aggregat (?) by the divine power, and from it comes the sapphire stone and golddust (or gold-bearing dirt). The roads, however, leading to this kind of thing but still more the wisdom by which they are prepared, the birds and and animals do not know nor either the braggards among men and the savages and they resemble the animals. To the rock he extended his hand, i.e., The wise man who first caused the rocks to be hewn because of many purposes: either for
buildings or for habitations or for (making) domiciles (of them (of the rocks cut into stones) or in them (i.e., caverns in the rocks) The whirlpool of the rivers he opened, i.e., It (this action of man) was the reason for the gushing forth of many rivers in the world because not all of them are from in the beginning but craftmanship by means of skill has made much of this kind.

All precious things, however, i.e., (used) of those (things) which were the reason for these, (i.e., the opening of the whirlpools and the making of rivers) or of those things in the earth and the sea and the air by (reason) which God is dear to men.

The depth of the rivers is revealed, i.e., That we may know that there is something in the depth of animal nature and of those without soul as pearls. He has demonstrated his power in (or by) the light, i.e., By means of the physical light he does all of it or: in the light of knowledge by which he (is able to) show his power in physical craftmanship.

Further: He demonstrates his power in (or by) the light, i.e., That he knew the cause of the light of the moon that it is from the sun and this light is the cause of all light. And later on while he wonders at the wisdom which is seen to be hid in the creation and at the mind which by means of intelligence and word was the cause that this wisdom which is seen in creation came into effect, he says: From where was wisdom found so that he (God) could put in nature this wisdom which is seen and discovered as to the works?
And this is God who brought and revealed the things obscure to the mind by the wisdom which he gave to us. Where is the place of wisdom? i.e., This (the wisdom) is not among men in a place, for you cannot say that it was in a place or that it was found in one of the created things and became known later on or that it is in a (certain) spot.

And he proclaims that man does not know its (Text: his) way, i.e., Not therein that he knows where it is and not in the creation and if this (wisdom) is thus, how, accordingly, can man venture to investigate the creator of this? (of the wisdom). Nor is it found in men, i.e., By nature it is not in them nor in the creation.

The abyss says it is not in me, i.e., In those material things--even if they are created by wisdom and wisdom is buried in them--yet that they should know, that by wisdom they are created or that wisdom is in them (this) is not to them, because it is granted to man alone. And when he later on enumerates all the precious things which are in the world and compares them to it (to the wisdom) then he says that it is superior to all of those things which are buried in the depth (?) and have not yet come into effect, silver, gold, beryl, sapphire, glass pearls, gems, jewels, etc., and he adds Wisdom, where is it found? i.e., And by this is it found he demonstrates the inexplorability of God who is (the) true wisdom and the inexplorability.

Further: of the multitudes of those things which are in the world which human wisdom has not yet been able to understand. Further: a man may say that not only to man is in the world many things which are unexplorable, but also to the birds of heaven, i.e., the angels, there is much which is unexplorable for them.

Hell and death say: We have not heard a rumor of it, i.e., This he says: Not that death destroys the wisdom of the wise ones by the separation of the soul from the body and the dissolution of this which takes place in the earth (that) which would not be wisdom, but he teaches that also in death and in hell wisdom is found because he who perished and was dissolved is going to rise (from the dead) to the praise of God and (also) he who is mingled with dust and in the sea, by the wisdom of God their parts are preserved unmingled with the elements. He imposes, however, upon the inanimate things and upon that which has no existence the shine of faculty to speak and of one speaking (?) and he says that he has found out that it (wisdom) is where it is not, i.e., In death and in solution wisdom is and also these (death and solution) are going to hear its praise when the parts are put together and he who was considered perished is gathered together.

Later on he demonstrates that God knows the weight of the earth as the cause and creator of everything visible and that he knows not only the things themselves as creator but also the weight and the measures of those things which
cannot be measured and that he saw it eternally before these (things existed) and explained it to us, for he told and taught us about it, naturally and prophetically and while he prepared it he prepared also for us that by wisdom we are able to know him and to investigate into his reasons. And he has further investigated (together) with us and--according to Job--has come to the opinion that fear of God is wisdom and that to keep away from evil is knowledge. Why? i.e., because that even if a man understands all knowledge in the created world as long as this does not lead him upwards toward me, the creator, he is not wise. And if it be that all these things lead upwards toward the creator, then we also learn about this (the creator) by means of those because therefore we are created as wise ones and find wisdom in the creation that we should know the creator.

What is the use of knowledge about him if it is that death destroys us? Also in man and in all the human world, however, is preeminence praised and evil hides itself, which according to wisdom we ought to examine and when we examine preeminence we find that the possession of wisdom is not for the sake of God only but also because of the life of the soul which comes after the solution, and the resurrection and the judgment because of which we should fear God.

And as to abstaining from evil (it is) because this is wisdom, as Job says: because it is doing us good and it saves us from the judgment, and it makes God glad for us. Who would place me in the former remnants, i.e., It refers
to how he was before the trials as to riches and good deeds toward the poor ones and also as to obedience of his servants and as to reverence of friends for him; and now because he has become poor and smitten he is despised by despicable ones and he relates the deeds of them and the obscurity (?) of them and of those who mock at him because God has opened his (God's) quiver and made it bad for him (Job).

And he threw upon him his arrows, i.e., The trials and the rest and he relates those things which are seen in effect upon him and he asks for death: If he could kill he would kill the one who--if there were another who would kill him when he commanded it--would not tarry from this (i.e., from commanding).

And he says while including in the speech about the trials the benefaction which he did and that he wept with all the weak ones and groaned over the pain of others and (then) he (the weak one?) cursed him later on. If it be that he had erred from the right way of the Lord or (that) he hid gold in his dust, i.e., buried it in the earth. Or relied upon precious stones or rejoiced in riches or urged the creditors and the like.

After this enters Elihu and he answers Job and his three friends and says that because he is young of years he kept quiet but now he is not (going to be) silent (any longer) as it is not the years that count (lit. speak) but the wisdom that God buried in the soul. And he blames the friends of Job because they did not answer him--for Elihu
thought that Job was tried rightly--and those who had been put to shame by him; and he promises that he will answer him and not be put to shame.

And he blames Job because he says that he is righteous and that God sent this against him, he being righteous and guiltless. And Elihu says that this is not found that God should not answer a man who is righteous. And he blames him further because Job said: Why does he not hear all the words of my case, as if Job wanted that he should answer each of the things that he said. And Elihu says that God speaks once, i.e., One time the Lord spoke to you in a blessing manner in that he made you spiritually free, Lord of a house, rich and king and similar things and he will not speak with thee again about those matters which you wish that they be answered to you one by one.

Lo, the answer is seen, i.e., You know what is right that God should answer you because you know his desire and the righteousness of his decisions and there is no need that he should speak with you because with (?) you, lo, he speaks because he has taught you his decision. And he adds: The second, however, by means of a dream (text: in the world) etc. i.e., With those plagues which are at you now, (and) which are due to your sins, he punishes you. They are a dream because he punishes you as a correction, then they pass (away) and you have no shame (from them). Or that God
punishes you with those has for you (the quality) of being grace (lit. that it is grace) for these are useful. Like the night they pass and (it is) in them (i.e., they have the power) that by reason of them your mind reveals to you that they are right inasmuch as they were the cause of your revertal from evildoing; according to the opinion of Elihu. That he fears (for) them, i.e., Those whom he (God) seeks to acquire and convert and to turn back from misdeeds and sin.

After this he speaks about what is seen in effect upon Job and he turns back again by means of this to what he heard from Job (i.e., Job's wish to return to his former state) and he comforts him with the hope of restoration if it be that he repents. And he blames him because he said that he does not deserve the plagues and he demonstrates that God is just and repays to everybody according to his deeds. And while he speaks much as well about the works of God and the incomprehensibility of his judgments as of his righteousness which is seen in the created world he shows that if it be, that on evidence from princes and kings, he who is poor cannot repudiate him who is powerful even if he is oppressed, but says to him: It is not right that you should quarrel with me, how then can man quarrel with God who is righteous and whose judgments are right.

After this the scripture relates and says: The Lord said to Job through a tempest and a cloud. And it is evident that this took place while his friends were present and listened. The scripture relates and says: The Lord said to Job
by means of a tempest and a cloud. And it is because that after Job had spoken and had reformed at that time the Lord spoke to the friends. By means of a tempest and a cloud the Lord spoke with him and not in a low voice of conversation as with Elijah because the Lord spoke as a correction of him and his friends and it is right that he should frighten them and make them tremble by the vision. These words namely were also spoken to Job himself, but Job did not conceal anything but revealed everything; accordingly those (things) were said (also) to the friends Elifaz, and Balded, and Zofar by the Lord when they had heard all of it. And it is evident that it was thus because when the Lord later on blames them he says to Elifaz: You have sinned and your two companions as you have not spoken the truth before me as (did) my servant Job.

div.head: The speech of God.
div.ab: Bind up like a warrior your loins, i.e., If you are able to stand up against me and be victorious, lo, I have revealed myself for thee as you desired; speak and I shall listen.

But Job was not able to do this for he had said to his friends: O, that he were with me or revealed himself to me, I should dispute with him on my case, but lo, God made this reality and he was not able to do this and he (God) asked him concerning the works which are to be seen in existence in the created world and the nature of their inherent power, that by which they came into existence from non-existence.
And he (God) is the one who supports them and they rest upon him. When I founded the earth, i.e., Its atomic parts; when I separated this (the earth) from the water and the rest of the elements all of them; I founded and made something, as it can be seen now, which is apt for dwelling (upon) etc. Tell me then if you know wisdom, i.e., If you are wise to the nature of these matters.

Who established its measure if you know it, i.e., Its length and width and its depth and its height, its kind and the heights which are upon it and the depths and its sphericalness. Further: Who established its measure? i.e., Made it, so as to become measurable; and thereby be fit to inhabitate; and some of it is inhabitable and some of it is mountains; also seas are upon it. Or who was the one who passed the rope over it? i.e., It is evident that God was this one, he it also was that made those things like the craftsmen who are among men. The rope, however, which he says that he passed over it, this is interpreted that like the masons and the craftsmen among us adjust and join (together) by means of a cord, thus he, God,--without materials and tools--made the earth in the center of a circle and it is the center so that it does not rise higher than the center and it does not bow downwards (from the center) and not to the four sides.

Its weight is fixed upon the water, i.e., Inasmuch as the earth thus is in the center of a circle, the water surrounds it on all sides and from above and from beneath
the air and the fire. And the firmament surrounds all of them in a spherical fashion. And if a man should say that they support each other he lies because there is nothing that supports anything except the power of God. And whether the elements cling to each other and the external heaven to them?--One may suppose so, but nothing can be said except that it is God's power which holds this and those and he supports all of them, they being not heavy upon him.

Who was the one who laid the stone as headstone of the corner upon it? i.e., Its foundation upon nothing and its corners on all sides which do not move (shiver) above the foundation. When the stars came into existence, (Text: When he....the stars) i.e., It is evident that the angels eulogized in all the six days, and because of all the works because they are affirmed (as being existent then) by the word of their creator. I barred the waters with a gate, i.e., Lest it should pass over and submerge that which is inhabited on this side; and (on) the other lest it should become dispersed; beneath you have dug for it depths in the earth upon which it stays. When it was born from its mother's womb it went forth, i.e., He represents the eternal prescience of God and the existence of these things in his knowledge in symbolical fashion by the womb and the mother.

But with fogs and clouds he said that he covered and enveloped, i.e., In as much as it (the sea) is the cause of these and these constantly are to be found in it (the sea); but one may also say that the fogs and the clouds are one of the gates and fetters of this (i.e., of the sea) because these (the clouds and fogs) do not permit it to be increased and pass over its original boundaries from the multitude of waters which enter it from the rivers, for (an amount) corresponding to as it is increased from the rivers is carried away from it by fogs and clouds that rise from it and is shed as dew upon the face of the earth.

Further: Fetters and gates are placed, i.e., Against the four original elements, for it is the divine power that does not permit one of them to be increased or decreased from from the original quantity and not to enter from one to another or to move from its natural place, not upwards and not downwards, and not to the left (and not to the right). And while they are locked up all of them in each other and there is not anything between them (it is) as if there were gates and fetters against each of them so that it cannot mix with the others, which is an expression to make it comprehensible; also he says: I have said up to here you may come and do not transgress etc.

The light of morning, i.e., that before the sun is seen the rays of its light are seen so that little by little the sight may be trained for it so that it (the sight) is not
hurt when it goes from the dark to the full view of its (the sun's) light. But the regularity of the morning-star he has seen, i.e., On all heaven and in each of the signs of the Zodiac there are stars who, when they are seen to start rising indicate (the coming of) the morning and the astronomers have names for them and by places and defined time it (the morning-star?) indicates morning according to it (i.e., the rules for it) and all of them rise from the wings of the earth and descend into its wings and they wake up those upon it and they also indicate the signs and the seasons as the Scripture says (Gen. I, 14.)

To push the wicked ones from it, i.e., All this order and beauty (?) and sleep and awakening, and light and darkness does not rise over good ones alone and benefit them but also over the wicked ones as well. And you, when I took the dust, i.e., You are not an exception to man (text: in the spirit of man). The one who rises up, however, and the wicked one he calls (text: i.e. he calls) the Accuser and the demons, those who in the beginning fell from the allegorical light of the angels because they became haughty. To the springs of the sea, i.e., Are you able to comprehend that natural cause, which does not permit it to diminish or can you come in ships until you arrive to its ends?

Have the gates of death opened themselves for you in fear? i.e., Are you able to arise from death to life? Or did the gates of Sheol shiver when they saw you? i.e., Are you capable when you as a soul (i.e., after your death) descend to
Sheol, that Satan and the demons and the souls who are confined in Sheol become horrified because of you? Like me (who) do this when I wish that which was fulfilled in the humanization of the Son. And he asks him to tell him how many stadia and miles or cubits the width of all the world is, i.e., that which man is not able to know.

But in which land does the light dwell? i.e., When it is above you do you know how much of the earth (it is) that it dwells above? Similarly when it departs from you know this very same which has been said? And before it comes to you, do you know from which land it has moved and (which) by the movement has become dark, and upon how much of it it dwelled?

Of the darkness, however, which is its place? i.e., Nor can man know this because the darkness is not locked up in a spot, nor has it any place because it is immaterial; it comes when the light moves away. If you brought me the boundaries of them, i.e., If you could say to me when the light is extended over you and it is day, until wherof the earth in length and width and depth the light marks the bounds of a place so that from this also the boundaries of the darkness would be known.

If then you know also the path to them, i.e., That you should wander the roads of the light which is now on the earth so and so many stadia and of the darkness. That then you were born, i.e., Did you know your existence when you were born or were you near to your soul like (you are) now?
Or do you know how much you were going to live? And he tells him later that he cannot see either how the snow and the hail are created in the clouds and that all of these he cannot bring when he wishes to. God makes them when he asks the accuser to take revenge or punish. Similarly (he does) not (know) either how he collects the snow and not how the wind is created or the cause of the rain or the nature of the thunder and lightning and the rest. i.e., Of Ice and of snow and of those misdeeds that are tortured by them (text: and of that they are tortured by them or not).

And the stars and heaven he mentions to him later on in order to teach him by them that he cannot comprehend the point of conjunction and the quantity of those and not the movement of the fix ones from place to place (or perhaps better: and that the fix ones do not move from place to place) or how by the various movements of the sun and the movements of the stars the seasons come to exist, summer and winter, etc. Nor, further, (does he know) the nature of the wisdom which has been implanted in us, by which women comprehend and perform the weaving of textures and all the rest that God brings.

Another one, however, who could do these things as he does, does not exist, for God descends (even) unto the animals and the birds that from them he may humiliate Job and teach him that his power and his knowledge is too small to that it should be able to comprehend the nature and qualities of them which are (to be) seen in them. And although they are made for the sake of man, some of them are not subject
to man because some of them were (i.e., remained?) servants after the sin (i.e., of Adam and Eve) and some of them were not servants.

Kanphai Shabican i.e., It is an allegory on the Synagogue. It gets many children and not for itself (for its own benefit) and also the Synagogue brought forth the Prophets and raised the Apostles and they left it and became children of the Church. It mocked at the horse and its rider, i.e., They laughed at the cross and at Christ who rode upon it.

Do you give the horse the mettle? i.e., A type of the holy people it symbolizes those things which are written concerning it. The falcon is the enemy of the birds and it symbolizes Satan, the enemy of the holy ones. Does the eagle rise up, a type of our Lord who was raised up upon Golgatha.

Its young ones suck up blood, i.e., From the blood of his cuts (?) the Gentiles, the young ones of Christ are benefited. This that he is going to catch the whale, i.e., This is called Leviathan and Tannim and is bigger than all the animals which God created upon the earth. And also it
is not able to live in the low and small seas but (it dwells) in the Ocean which is sufficient that it may turn itself; and the size of the body of each of them exceeds more than 1000 stadia and a stadion makes 4000 cubits. And the measure of one of the old ones exceeds 200 miles and a mile is 7 stadia and a half. This (animal) is mocked at by the angels according to the words of David and God alone can hold it according to the word of Job. This that it is mocked at by the angels means that they wonder at its great size and (at the same time) they see that it is bitten by the (smaller) animals of the sea and it writhes and is in pain. It is a picture of the Accuser, who is going to be bound by Christ in the end.

Kanphai Shabichan, i.e., It is a bird and it has strength but is deprived of intelligence. And it brings forth its eggs on the earth so that they are fractured lest its progeny shall become numerous upon the earth and destroy the human beings; and in its strength it can snatch away a horse and the rider who is upon it and fly away. And it dwells in the place of the Hindues and when it grasps something in its claws it cannot release them for a long while. It perishes when it falls into the sea. And when people (lit. they) want to catch it, they bring a chariot and they heap up upon it a pile of stones and bind to it bulls and when it descends and thrusts its claws in the bull it cannot take it away because of the heaviness of the chariot and its claws cannot get loose because they penetrate to beneath the bones of the oxen and they fetch it immediately.

Lo! an animal with teeth (a ferocious animal?) is with you, i.e., This animal that is with you which he mentiones is the grasshopper, and it is called among the Hebrews Behemoth, numerous animals. This (animal) eats green herbs like a bull doing harm to the seedcorn and it possesses power in its loins and in the navel of its belly, and it dwells upon stones and thorns and is not hurt, and it moves and raises its tail like a cedar, and it jumps upon the earth like the quadrupeds (lit. wandering animals) and flies like the strong birds. And the body on its loins and side is tough like dense sinews and its ribs are like brass and the bone of its loin is like iron and it is the head of the creation of God because in the springtime it jumps and goes out before all the herbs and plants of the field, and it grows big (numerous) little by little.

This (animal) makes war with men and animals snatching away their food and God made it to be wondered at and admired and for the joy of the angels, those who direct it, and it does not turn from its (mutual) unanimity and it runs in one (single) direction like the water which flows down in one direction. And it comes upon the side (?) of the mountains which support it (?), and it is not harmed and gladdens the animals when they nourish from it and also the reptiles when it fells into cavities and swamps, and it lies down under the trees and reeds and canes and upon trees and the birds which eat it surround it. It is not harmed either by the river, but when it wanders it binds itself together and rides
upon each other like a bridge and brings over its comrades as a bridge without injury because it trusts that it shall endure the vehemence of the river in front of its nose, when it flows before its eyes as the scripture says.

Concerning this grasshopper, God says to Job: You have not the power that you can vanquish it and if you cannot vanquish this, how can you speak before God. After this Job answers and says: What shall I answer thee? (text: Have I been judged) i.e., and in these (words) he shows the smallness of his strength and the greatness of the strength of God, who blamed him. And he shows his humility and confesses that he is not able to answer God and the Lord answered and said to Job who had his inferiority: Do not speak thus, but bind up like a hero your hips, i.e., Show yourself firm if you can answer me when I ask you; and he shows by his words that therefore he has revealed himself to him and speaks with him that he may teach him that he cannot vanquish the divine strength in a dispute. And also for this reason he revealed himself to him that he might show him to be right. That which he said to him: Is there to you an arm like God? They mean the same things which have been said before even (if?) they are different in wording (?). He teaches him by those (words) that he cannot become like God.

Others call Leviathan Behemoth; that which he says that it is the head of the creation of God they explain; with reference to the whale which is bigger than all the animals of the sea and the dry land he calls it thus or because it
was created on the fifth day, before the ferocious animals on the sixth day or because it was created to be admired for its great size. It is laughed at by the angels because they wonder at it. People say that the clouds lift this one, which is that strong, up to places inside of Cush that it may become food for a strong people.

Further: laughter can be taken in two senses in the scripture, as joy and as disdain and wonder as here and as Sarah laughed, i.e., She wondered how this could be (possible) and the Lord rebuked her laughter, i.e., her wondering and said that it was possible. The Gentiles which are nourished by it, i.e., the Phoenicians. And he adds that Job cannot put his hand upon it and if this Leviathan used to move according to its nature no one would be able to live in the sea because of its strength, nor on the dry land if it used to come up, and for that reason it was created in the sea, in the sea because a size like this would not have been able to exist on the dry land, but would have destroyed everything.

People say that one of them went out in the sea in Phoenicia at Beiruth and others say that (it was) in the sea of Egypt and when the people noticed it they started to cut and eat of its flesh and after a while it felt it and departed and from where this was and until the beginning of its body they measured that it was 300 miles long besides the width which they were not able to get (?).

And thereafter Job demonstrates his inferiority and the greatness of God and God rebukes the friends of Job because they did not speak the truth, for they considered Job sinful and wicked and (thought) that he was smitten because of his iniquity. And he commanded that they should make sacrifices and purify themselves because (lit. from) they had sinned against him.

And God blessed Job and gave him double of everything that had perished with the exception of sons and daughters, so that the later conditions became like the former. For they, his sons who dies, were alive for God and did not perish like the possessions and wealth.
And this he did to him that everybody should know that he was punished, not because of his sins, but as a temptation (in which) he vanquished the Accuser.

Completed is the book of the righteous Job, the literal
commentary in brevity, and pray for Monseigneur
Dionysious the late who collected and
gathered (the material for the
commentary) and for the un-
worthy scribe Matthias
the Diacon.

div.head: Bar Salibi, Metaphysical Commentary
div.ab: One more commentary--a metaphysical namely and physical--of the book of Job according to the Peshitta version and it is the second commentary.

Job.- Sometimes he is a symbol of our Lord and sometimes of the world and at other (times) of Adam. A simple and righteous man. A type of the one (Christ) who did not commit sin neither was any deceit found in his mouth. Seven sons were born unto him. The Prophets, the Apostles, the Teachers, the Performers of miracles (?) those who have received healing, the helpers, the leaders. Three daughters; a type of the pure souls. That he cursed the day he was born. By the day he symbolizes the people of the Hebrews. May it not be reckoned among the number of the days. A type of the people which is not reckoned with the believing gentiles. Stars that grow dark he calls the leaders of the people.

The wife of Job.- A type of Eve; she urged him to curse God like Eve urged Adam that he should eat from the tree. His friends came to him and they knew him not. As no one knew the son when he had been incarnated and had been surrendered. Before (this) Job says thus: Perhaps my sons have sinned or contempted, i.e., everybody accordingly should fear evil thoughts and should pray against them. Amidst the sons of God Satan came; accordingly we should fear (even) at the time of prayer because the enemy is not
far from us. The sons of God are the holy ones; that Satan came amidst them does not mean that he wanted to pray but (it was) in order to hold them back from the prayer. That the fire fell: it was Satan; he took the likeness of fire and consumed them. Spare his soul, i.e., his intellect from which the thoughts are borne.

Naked I went out from the womb, It is a type of the Spostles who abstained from possessions and like this: Nothing we have brought into the world etc. Job, that he was smitten with ulcers. A type of Adam who was destroyed by Satan and smitten with sin. There is hope to the wood, An example to the fact that he will return to health and of the human nature in general which blooms from the wind of baptism and is renewed and produces green leaves. This: His path is obscure, he says of the path of death because it is hidden from men. This that God hedges him in, means that he delivers him by means of death from pains and adversities. If I should devote myself to discussing with you, you would become irked, i.e., At the beginning of his speech he charges him with impatience that he may compel him to moderation and willingness to understand (a different viewpoint). And who can stop your words, i.e., I do not like to do this, but I cannot endure your words lest I should be punished like you.

Who have indulged in vain glory, lo! You have punished many In the measure with which he has measured he is repaid, i.e., They (or the words) are fulfilled upon the accuser, the sentence of righteousness further passes over to (i.e., reaches) him (as) symbolized by the bow of brass. And his intestines are torn out and brought forth, that those whom he has consumed shall not remain in his interior. The food which he has consumed he must vomit up again. They were silent and did not answer him. It symbolizes the silence which (was) extended over the prophecies when Immanuel revealed himself.

I shall (not) decide in the favor of man and from the face, i.e., It is fulfilled upon God because there is no favoring with him and he does not know shame because he does not sin. Also I have been molded from clay, i.e., Because it is assimilated to us and takes from us the body he is similar to clay. Because once God speaks and a second time he does not add thereto. With the perfect he speaks as with Moses, with those who are below the perfect in a vision as with Ahron and Miriam. And his flesh is changed (to) as in his youth. Adam who returned to his former ideal state.

The humble is rescued by his humbleness. This means that all men are repaid according to their deeds and if he has behaved humbly he is saved from the judgment. He will lay open ways for them in the pain. It states
the salvation of the holy ones. And he will prepare a table full of fat things. It symbolises the good things which the holy ones get in this world. He shows his friends his possessions, also the evil ones, i.e., This symbolises the apostles who here in part have received the gift of the tongues in the new world they shall see his possession which is the splendor of his kingdom while he is doing good to them with it copiously. The rascals he torments while they see the righteous in happiness. He brings down much water, i.e., The rain--allegorically--upon the earth of the soul. And he disperses the clouds of his light. It has reference to allegorical clouds.

He circles and turns himself to carry out thoughts, i.e., Not like (it is) the habit of a drivers he circles around and turns, but it has reference to (the fact) that he reveals himself to his holy ones in visions which are not alike so that although he is one, the ideas regarding him are many because of the diversity of forms in which he is revealing himself.
And he has closed the gate of the sea. The great gate of the labor of the angels which is made manifest to us in the spirit was closed within a covering up of our material sight.

And he let (it) flow forth from the womb and let (it) out while he placed.... i.e., The womb is explained as the divine will, for therein (all) creatures were formed and molded and it engendered them, and from its womb they went forth.

He made the clouds its garment and gloom its swaddling-band, i.e., Even if a little of a person might be seen in the gloom, yet (it is impossible to see the divine will, for) the cloud is placed inside the gloom, and while we might see the clouds, our sight is not able to see inside of the cloud. Gloom, however, is something like a cloud (lit. is asemi-cloud, a half-cloud) like mist, namely that.......(?) which is placed upon the earth in the form of darkness, so that out sight is not able to see what is inside the cloud of fire which surrounds God. The cursers of the day may curse it, i.e., The righteous who curse the day upon which they were born.

Those who are ready to wake up Leviathan, The righteous may curse it, (those) who are going to seek revenge from Satan who is symbolized by Leviathan (lit. who is the allegorical Leviathan). When you have instructed many why do you not punish yourself? Your words did not upholden the weak, i.e., Those who were weak in spirit did not understand the power of your words; and the words of our Lord were not able to upholden the weak in the Jewish religion because of their craftiness.

Cry, I pray, if there is any who will answer you, and with whom of the holy...., i.e., When God has left you nobody can save you from the punishment, and with whom of the holy have you encountered a (God)-forsakenness like this? For I have seen that the rascals grew (but then) perished, i.e. Even if a rascal grows and is not punished like you, know, that his perdition will come suddenly.

Man was born to toil as the winged ones. i.e. Not as those who lift the wing, who are the winged ones who are the angels. Because of the fact that he is under punishment man is born in pain and is subject to toil. He taketh the wise! i.e. Concerning the demons he says that they are taken in their (own) craftiness, those whom (the demons) he calls the crafty; and in the very thing they believe they have been victorious in, in this they are defeated.

In the daytime they grope as ... i.e. Daytime he calls the new world, in which the demons are delivered up to darkness. And the chastisement of the mighty one he does not despise. i.e. I have watched how he is tried (and I found) that he has endured it excellently. Six troubles he calls the six years of the temptation and In the seventh that in which he was worthy of remuneration. Elifaz said this word as a prophecy.

If I were washed with waters of snow. Waters of snow he calls the doctrine of Satan, with which Job has not anointed himself at all, and he demonstrates, that he who shall wash himself with these waters removes from himself the
garment of righteousness and he plunges himself into the abyss (lit. the cavern) of destruction.

In skin and body thou hast clothed him. By this he symbolizes the incarnation of our Lord, who is of our nature, and they are spoken as if by the person of the son to the father. He reveals the depths from the darkness and leads out. It is likely that (it refers to) that which Isaiah said of Immanuel: He said to the prisoners: Go out and to the bound ones: Show yourselves. (Isaiah 49.9) And with the strength of his hands he bound me. The hands of God are the people, for with it as with hands he fought the Canaanites, and when the son had revealed himself in flesh, his body was bound by the hands of the people, i.e., his hands and his feet were pierced and his loins were fractured.

Now I know that from death you will bring me back. The son says to the house and the church. That after his incarnation he went up to his father. Further the word expresses a praise of the resurrection. Who hates the strife shall not be victorious. The one who fears the strife with evil and flees from the flight with Satan throws away the crown which is given to those who vanquish the accuser. Who used to fear the hoarfrost upon them is much snow. Who used to fear the Jews and the veneration of idols their error has
become abundant like the snow which is more abundant than the hoarfrost, but if the rays of the cross radiated to them instantly they would melt away.

Until when will you (continue to) speak those things, a spirit of vanity (being). When Job spoke truthfully the second friend, Bildad, considered his words haughtiness. A type of those who considered Immanuel a sinner. He has made my wounds many without reason. Inasmuch as he is punished without having sinned he symbolizes also Christ who without having dealt wrongly received bodily pains.

He gave the earth in the hands. Earth he calls the body which was delivered over to Satan but judges his thoughts. Allegorically he calls the spirit, earth; when it is delivered over and given into the hand of the accuser all understanding of righteousness is covered up from (lit. in front of) its thoughts. He calls the right thoughts judges. For I know that my deliverer lives and in the end he shall be seen on earth. End he calls the fulfilling of the prophecy that in the last days Christ will rise.

The division of the rivers of butter and honey which Sophar mentioned. As is the false opinion of the heathens
and the Jews he said that they shall not see them; the apostles however, while sucking learning from the one of whom is written that butter and honey he shall eat, give, spiritually, drinks to the gentiles.

And his hand killed the fleeing serpent. i.e. Christ killed with pain the serpent, the accuser. Fleeing he is called because he flew from with the angels. You will bring to me the blessing of him who has perished. i.e. For perished he is, the one who, when he perished for the world and those who are of it, was found by God as he says: He who loses his life (lit. soul) for my sake shall find it.

The ear tried words. For ear he calls the intellect to which belongs the examination of words, for from the ear is hearing but from the intellect, thoughts. He made the stars of morning at the same time and all the sons of the angels shouted for joy. For even if it be (granted) that people may understand it as referring to allegorical matters yet it is not meet that the angels should be considered as possessing the state of sons but we understand the morning (as) Christ but the stars (as) the apostles, the sons of the angels further (as) the teachers.

And he held back the doors of the sea. i.e. For the hurricanes of erring. And he made flow forth from the womb and he led it out when he placed.... i.e., he placed in the womb of baptism a power of immortality and he led out from it also. He made the cloud its garment, i.e., the elements. And the vapor has encircled it. A covering which keeps it
from diminishing the vapor.
The wild ass is a symbol of the accuser who was left a free man and is not subjected to the yoke of righteousness as (are) the angels.

Who made the plain its house. i.e. The heart of those who are held back in earthly things even if Cain took Abel out to the plain when he wished to kill, i.e., to the house of the accuser who is the wild ass. And in the salt-region its dwelling. i.e. In the mind, destitute of good fruits. The unicorn is a symbol of the mind. It has one horn as the desire of the mind is one (the one) which goes upward.

He let a spirit pass before me. i.e. Something like a spirit passed by me. He felt it in a desert place. A sound and a voice he calls the thoughts. Is man made righteous by God? (No!) but from his (own) free will. His servants he does not trust. i.e. The angels. His angels he charges with admiration. i.e. That they are not victorious before him.

They are not established as inhabitants for eternity. i.e. They perish, those who expected that they would remain forever. And not in wisdom. i.e. In that foolishness that they expected that they would be heirs for eternity. Envy (is) rebuke. Because with the stones of the plain your covenant shall be. i.e. With the just he will upholden you with God.

Oh! that my punishment was weighed! i.e. That it might be seen that the punishment has not killed me like the fool according to your word. But even harder than the sand. i.e. The punishment cannot be weighed. My words are kept back. i.e. Thereby that they are not received by you as truth. The vengeance of God, he calls the affliction.

Does the wild ass snort upon the grass? i.e. That if the wild animals guard their lives I (would have done the same) if not for his arrows. And to me a word was brought secretly. i.e. I have received from my fathers that the wicked is repaid according to his wickedness and the righteous according to his righteousness. Fodder he calls straw.

He frightened me in dreams. i.e. Not even in sleep in which is rest for toil there was relaxing for me. They passed with the ships. i.e. As the path of a ship cannot be distinguished in the sea. And you change the armies against me. i.e. Like a general changes his troop when it is tired.

To your words the dead ones (only) will be silent. i.e. Because those who are alive like me will not suffer them. Passing waters. i.e. He calls the afflictions water. Oh! That you had hidden me in Sheol. i.e. From this hard punishment.

Is it true that a strong mountain falls? i.e. Like a mountain does not fall, my sins will not irritate you. You strengthen him forever. i.e. He believes that he stands by his (own) power, you (however) are the one who has established him firmly forever. Do you not count my steps? Who is man that he should be pure? i.e. The holy ones are few and when (although) they are holy they are not holy.

He broke me breach upon breach. i.e. After the news of his sons and his property also that which was in his body. I was cast down and he tore me off. i.e. By the plagues of pains and the stories which were (current) about him. He has erected me as a target for arrows. i.e. For his hard beatings. The earth will not cover my blood. i.e. The pus which came from him. And there was no place for my cries. i.e. It indicates his prayers and his alms.

They have dealt falsely like brooks and like rivers. i.e. The water of brooks and rivers come down from heaven and does not stay long because they (the brooks and rivers) dry up. In this manner types were sent to the people by means of the cloud, namely, the prophets, and the gift departed from
them like brooks which disappear and dry up from (being full of) water.

Who is sitting between the roads. i.e. Satan. The wild ass. The serpent, the demons who in insolence run to destroy the sould of the holy ones. Not shall he rejoice in the dividing of the streams. i.e. On Golgatha the streams are divided, namely, the gifts of the spirit. My skin and my flesh he pressed against my bones. i.e. His flesh he has pressed, and his whole body became liquid from the pressure. (Read Text: body, )
And with a writing-cane of iron and a stylus which passes. i.e. As the remembrance of the alms will not (be) forgotten before him, thus likewise my words were written.
See the light, my kidneys! i.e. Those (upon) whom as they do not partake in the deeds of darkness he (Satan) throws upon them an arrow and he feels no compassion.

I have become their delight, they contempt me, etc. i.e. By this he shows how the Jews enkindled themselves against Immanuel and did not hold spit back from his face. For I have perished from my pact. i.e. He rebukes them: I have not denied my pact or ceased from it according to as you say that because I have contaminated the pact of God I am not saved. They have made me like unto clay. i.e. Christ because he was despised. The Jews said to him while thou art (only) a human you have made yourself God.
I have become like unto dust. i.e. Of earthen nature. The word became flesh. This however: Like ashes is because he became an abomination instead of us.

Why do the wicked ones live? i.e. He gives good things to the wicked to show that he does not hate them lest they should say: He hates us and has not opened for us the gates of conversion. He brings to the righteous ones pains to show his love to them and the retribution of their good things.

Lo, not was their luck by their hands. i.e. That it was not from their works that they acquired their luck. And the evil barren woman will give birth. i.e. For this is the soul which is thinking on evil and it is called barren because it has closed its womb and has not accepted the seed of the doctrine of life. And I have fled with the skin of my teeth. i.e. I was left a corpse.

And he did not remember the one who established their foundations. i.e. When the spies (lit. explorers) feared the people they did not remember him who with hard punishments bore and brought them forth. Today my anxiety is bitter. i.e. From my anxiety bitter things spring up for me. Fodder he calls straw. hᵉlamtha is myrrha or bugloss. My brethren have dealt treacherously. i.e. Like brooks in which was water, which are filled in the winter and are empty in the summer. The confidence in them. i.e. That by his riches they were attracted to him and in his temptation they drew back from him.

They looked at the roads to Teima. i.e. To much wealth and good things which had come from Ophir and Sheba. They were put to shame by something they had been enthrusted. i.e. Because everything is nothing. The mighty, he calls God. Turn, I pray, now. i.e. Turn.

And he measures the evening. i.e. He speaks of hours and spaces of time. I was restless. i.e. I asked (prayed). Shudders. i.e. Contracts and diminishes itself. The spirit is living. i.e. The soul because it is not dissolved.

Am I a sea or a serpent since you establish. i.e. To the sea he established the sand as a boundary lest it should overflow and inundate the earth and (to) the serpent the external cloud and it keeps it back lest it should attack and destroy many. But I am weak and earthly, what is the reason that you have taken me captive by this punishment?

You have horrified me. i.e. You have frightened me. In the morning. Of the shortness of the adversities and the times of evening of the end of the adversities. He likened him to papyrus and reeds. When the reed has thrown its fruit then it is cut off like you: After you have given fruits you die and are destroyed. And from the dust another grows up. i.e. Like from dust the righteous grows in his humility.

He who turns around the southwind. He speaks of the
wind which blows from the south. If he passes me I am not seen by him. This that his affliction covered his limbs like a shield and even if he passes by me I am not seen by him (I do not see him). God does not turn his wrath from the wicked. The helpers of many are humiliated. i.e. Those who in their righteousness are able to help many. If I am perfect and he deals unjustly with me. i.e. Even if I considered myself without a spot (defilement) I must appear untrue with him because of the punishment which is upon me.

And you made ready your weapons against me. i.e. In the likeness of fighters who fix (direct) their weapons against each other. There is an inner side of wisdom. i.e. Either he says that wisdom is deep or that it is abolished (lit. has been wrapped up) and has ceased. Are you able to understand the end of the mighty? i.e. Do you understand something of the Almighty, or do you understand the perfection of the works which he performs.

An innocent man is encouraged. i.e. By God. And he who is strong helps man. i.e. He who is strong by fear of God is able to help others. And from the pit midday will arise. i.e. Midday () he calls the affliction; that from the affliction you will get release.

Keep away from you the threats of God. i.e. As much as your words are strong thus thy afflictions are painful. Neck he calls the hard neck. My enemies fixed their eyes toward me. Like this that they rejoiced at those things which have happened to me.

He has delivered me up to the evil angel. i.e. Satan who without mercy has smitten me. He has shed my gall upon the earth. i.e. His flesh has putrefied. My gall he calls his flesh, that which has been constantly smitten with evil ulcers. The earth will not cover my blood. i.e. So that the cry of this blood may go up from the earth and his severe punishments may not be covered in it. Or that it should not be covered but should be on a smooth stone for remembrance. There would not be place for my cries. i.e. That they are not answered.

My witnesses are in Heaven. i.e. His prayers and alms. They make night to day. i.e. You call the evil good. (Comp. Is. 5.20) We are considered like (wild) beasts. i.e. Because Job said to them: I have not found a wise one among you.

Is the soil left because of you? i.e. Like this: Were you the only one who cultivated it? The mountain moves from its place. i.e. By the hurricane of your sin. Also the lamp of the wicked shall be extinguished. i.e. Adversity will suddenly come upon them. Also the flame shines.
i.e. That the punishment will stay upon him some time. ( belongs after lit. a space of time.) The thirsty ones deal harshly with him. i.e. Pains and sickness. He has torn out my hope like wood. i.e. Which is delivered over to be burned when it is cut.

A prophecy of Job's: I know that my deliverer lives and in the end he shall reveal himself upon the earth. i.e. He will converse with us physically (lit. bodily) as a human. Who is the one who will deliver him over (in) my hand. If there be any who wishes to contend with me, viz., (holds) that these my words are not true, deliver him in my hands and let him come to me, that we may see the words how much they are true.

The praise of the wicked is of their midst. i.e. That they praise themselves is as much as they are not praised by others. The gall of the serpent he must suck. Viper he calls the snake, i.e., like the gall of the viper is the heir of predatory riches and like the tongue of the adder the wealth which he has gathered kills him. He cannot swallow because of the force of its metamorphose (of the bread cf. v.15) i.e. In the same way that a man cannot swallow anything that
is not eatable, thus he cannot either keep something which he has gathered as spoil.

Fire is not blown. i.e. Which is not extinguished. Hear attentively my words. i.e. You, expects that you can teach others. Endure with me in your integrity (good health) as you have endured (read perhaps: as I have endured) in my pains. If I remembered I was horrified. i.e. The wicked who sin and are unconcerned; why are they joyous and grow old and are not horrified? And the curve of the river consumes him. i.e. The evil adversities of Sheol and death.

That which the deceitful people continued (fault for wandered) who out of time. i.e. The deeds of those ancient ones you imitate. It has reference to those of Cain's house and the Sodomites, these he calls the ways of the people. Who out of time. i.e. Who in what was not their right time. They were kept back by the passing of the river. i.e. They were cut off from their evil deeds by means of the river of pains which passed over them.

They did not remember the one who laid their foundation. i.e. Who planted their foundations. What the evildoers suppose (to happen) (lit. the opinions of the evildoers) is far from them. i.e. They think that they will end their days among good things; but disaster comes suddenly over them.

Combine yourself with him, (or If he had made himself worthy of him). i.e. Acquire equality to the love which is with God. Also today my complaint is bitter. i.e. In your ears, or that from my complaint bitterness springs up for me. There I used to strive righteously with him. i.e. In that judgment that I have been condemned today by you.

And like the wild asses in the wilderness. i.e. The wicked ones rob first the food of the poor to fulfill their desires. This For their young ones. i.e. He takes as reference to their wildness, that like food is pleasant (or useful: Necessary) to the young ones, thus also robbing to them. And on the field fodder. i.e. Fodder is said of seed which has been trampled and tread out and whose straw has been blown away empty (lit. light).

The vineyard of the wicked they glean. i.e. That it is not sufficient for the wicked ones that they rob the poor, but they (the poor) work for them without wages. In the house of festivals they recline. i.e. Those poor ones are the cause for those that they can eat (celebrate) the festival. From the midst of the village dead ones sob. i.e. To this state of humiliation they have come by the hands of the wicked that they are like dead ones and murdered ones and cry like sick people.

They have sinned in Sheol and have erred from the womb. He has turned the sentence around. Thus he wishes to say: From the womb they have erred in Sheol, i.e., that
from when they went forth from the womb they have been committed (lit. employed) to sin, therefore, they have fallen into the shadow of death. Lo! The moon cannot be innocent and the stars are not clean before him. i.e. This is not said in the physical sense because the moon and the stars do not do good deeds nor bad ones but it is said of the righteous ones, that they are not able to (stand as) pure ones before God because they are subject to the sentence of Adam. Further, it is said of Abel.

Heroes are killed. i.e. Of those who perished in the deluge he says that because they have committed iniquity they were suffocated (drowned). And the strong ones who spoke to my soul. i.e. Through his pains. And he held it back in me. i.e. So that it could not get away and go to rest.

To the silver there is (a place) where it comes out. i.e. The places where it comes from are known. And on (a definite) place they find the gold. i.e. Because with water they (have to) wash and purify the gold. And iron is melted out of dust. i.e. Thus God concealed the gold and the silver and the other species in the likeness of stones and placed them in the earth. The stone of the cave. i.e. Cave he calls the abyss; likewise as the gold, etc. are concealed in the earth, thus, there is upon it righteous and sinners.

They are forgotten from the streams and are declared
untrue by men. i.e. They are torn off by the punishment as by a stream and they go out to destruction and are forgotten. They are declared untrue, which he says means that they are rooted out from men and become few (or insignificant). And they have laid bare the earth, from which goes out foods (victuals). i.e. By means of work and by means of seed-corns which are sown in it.
pᵉtawtka (a certain precious stone), i.e., variegated. Dahna (for dahia: splendent), i.e., pure. Calchedon Stone, i.e., gold-colored.

He made a law for the rain. i.e. When it should go down. Oh, that I were as in the former months. i.e. Like the months before he came upon me with that of the six, or as the first month of the year, magnificent in flowers and blossoms. And (that) like the days of God, he guarded me, i.e., like the days in which God guarded me.

He has made his fear above my head. i.e. That it be like a crown upon my head. He extended him lamp over me. i.e. In the darkness he lighted for me. In his light have I walked in the dark. i.e. When he extended over me the light of his lamp he also lightened (illuminated) the darkness for me.
Old men rose and wondered at me. i.e. (At) how I suffered the afflictions. The voices of princes grew hard. (lit. hid themselves) i.e. In horror from rapacity.
An ear who heard my praise. i.e. Concerning something I had performed in longsuffering of my afflictions. In truth I clothed myself and it covered (lit. clothed) me. i.e. Among errant ones.

Adversity is the yoke of the evildoer. i.e. Job says this as if in the name of Christ who conquered death and took it captive. I shall be completed as a reed. i.e. As the Read which is (the constellation), Libra (the scales) in justice and truth or as a reed which grows high at the water thus also I shall grow in the fear of God.

Like a shadow shall stay overnight. i.e. This shadow is dew; likewise, as a field upon which falls during the night is inundated and ripens for the harvest (lit. attains the time of harvest), thus I hope that I shall get good things in abundance (lit. be filled with good things) until I shall die. I shall be refreshened, i.e., from coolness. Another man (reads) I shall be invited, I shall come because that which has been called (also) comes.

My bow is changed in my hand. i.e. To disaster. They waited for me as for rain. i.e. They hoped that also for me deliverance would come as (they would hope) for rain for those who hoped for it. Examine your ways. i.e. Your thoughts.

They have bound my feet. i.e. With their derision. From my youth pains reared me. i.e. From the beginning I have been troubled about (being) excellent while I was reared by pains and sighs for the sake of those in pain. My shoulder may fall from its place. i.e. From its joints. If I have seen the light when it arose, etc. i.e. That even if they are praiseworthy and splendid and magnificent yet they are (only) creations of you.

My hand has kissed my mouth. i.e. By means of a bribe. With your words I shall (not) answer him. i.e. I shall judge him with silence, or he says that his sins have awakened (God's wrath against him. Lo, my womb is in pain. i.e. The womb is the soul. And it is not opened. i.e. By a revelation. Like a fruit is cleft in the month. i.e. In the likeness of a fruit ripens in its (appointed) time, thus, also I send out words at their right time. And my violence may not be heavy upon thee. i.e. My words.
He who hates the strife will not be victorious. i.e. He who hates persecution and punishment and murmurs will not be victorious. They were false. i.e. They are right and conform to the truth.

He says to the snow: Be earth. i.e. When it comes down upon the earth it is trampled upon like the earth. From the chamber, i.e., the will of God. Comes the storm, i.e., strong wind. From the breath of God. i.e. Calling the wind
breath; from the cold comes up hoarfrost. Hᵉsida i.e., mercy like (in) this (passage) my mercy shall not pass away from him (II Sam. 7.15). They burn, i.e., they are warm.

I will ask you; answer me! i.e. For you have asked this that you might come unto the throne of my glory and speak your case over before me; lo! I have come to you that you may investigate me, not my nature (however) which cannot be investigated by creation that you should not become the cause for many later on that they would master the examining of their creator although (they should master only the examining of) the creation, your equal and the earth which carries you.

The sons of the angels shouted for joy. i.e. They wondered, those who saw the creation being put in order. He closed the gates of the sea, i.e., he established for it the sand as a limit and it does not transgress it. And he let it flow forth from the womb. i.e. In the likeness of a child who, when it comes out of the womb, is enveloped in swaths, thus he also bound the sea in the bosom of the earth after it had come
into existence. Cloud and mist he calls the invisibility and incomprehensibility of his decisions. Who engendered the helmet of heaven? i.e. Heaven he calls the air (it means): the denseness (text: holiness) of the air from which the clouds are condensed; who made that?

The unicorn is not persuaded to work for thee. i.e. In this those who do not submit to the work of this world are vituperated. The unicorn, however, has one horn like the righteous whose truth is one. The sinews of the loins (text: Banquet) of Behemoth he calls those strong sinews which are on the two sides of the neck. In Behemoth, namely the grasshopper, Satan is depicted. He calls him the head of creation because as the first he fell in sin.

The Tannin; namely, the whale, Do you pierce its jaw? i.e. Are you able to pierce its jaw and to throw in it a nose-string and a nose-ring? i.e., he binds it like a bird upon which the kids have thrown a string. Do you fill its skin (with) flesh? i.e. Do you skin it and throw its flesh in its skin? And do you cook it in the shadow of the fire like a ram? And do you put your hand upon it? i.e., your sway.
Lo! Your foot is free, i.e., Lo! he permits you to do everything you wish. And God has removed its bitterness. i.e. And God help you quieting its bitterness.

The walls of its teeth are like fear in the valley. i.e. If a man looks into its mouth it is as if he (lit: He
is not different from the one who) looks into a deep valley. The wall of its teeth, i.e. the gums of its teeth. For its mouth is closed and sealed, i.e., from humiliation(?). And like torches go out naturally from its mouth and its breath burns like glowing embers. And from its nostrils smoke goes out.

And like a brazier of a kettle, i.e., like vapor. Sparkels of fire. Zunama is a stone which is black of color. It goes around on dust. i.e. He calls the earth dust and it goes around in the abyss (sea) as upon the earth.

Seven sons were born unto him (Job) and three daughters and he called the first Imama (Daytime). Now my pains have passed away and relaxing has come to me as the daylight. And the second Qeso a, i.e., from in the midst of my death grew up for me new life and you have broken and killed the accuser. The third Qarnapokh, i.e., my horn has been filled more than before and I have returned to strength. By the names of the sons and the daughters (by this) that he does not name them (the sons), he shows that he gave equal honor to the women as to their brothers and forgiveness to their mother, who had sinned for her blasphemy.

Further concerning Behemoth: This an animal with teeth is with you; she whom I have made (to be?) with you
(is) Behemoth; like a bull it eats herbs. Its power and strength is upon its loin, etc. i.e., This strong and by force unconquerable animal is the grasshopper; and Behemoth may be read as a plural, i.e., many animals. And it may be read as a singular: The grasshopper, because of their unanimity, although they are divided in many individuals. This one eats herbs like a bull, doing harm to the seed. And it has power upon its loin and strength upon the navel of its womb; and when it jumps upon stones and trees and thorns, it is not hurt in its body. And its tail stands up like a ceder, and it jumps like the animals upon the earth and again it flies like a bird. And it is strong like brass and its backbone is like iron, and it is the head of all the creation -- those who spring up and grow in the time of the spring -- because it goes forth first and grows big little by little against the growth of the field. And God made it to fight with the humans and the animals in eating their food, and God established it to be a wonder and a mockery for the angels, those who lead it and look after it that it shall not leave off from the fight and from the unanimity with its comrades but tend in one direction like the course of the waters.

And it comes upon the sides of the mountains and the rocks and it cannot be debarred, and it causes joy to the animals and to the reptiles and to the fishes when it alights on, or falls in, ditches and rivers, and the birds feed on them (the grasshoppers) both the ravens and the magpies. And it wanders and swims upon the water and it binds (itself to
gether into something) like a bridge to bring over its comrades and it trusts that it will endure the vehemence of the river (that is) before its eyes while it is swimming.
Of this one God says to Job: You do not possess its strength in battle. How can you then speak against God and expect to be victorious?

Finished is the spiritual commentary on the
righteous Job.

p. 44, n. 2 The first of the two theories on Job's genealogy, which Bar Salibi mentions is the one generally accepted in the early church. It is found in the addition to the book of Job in LXX and was held by men like Origenes Irenaus, Eusebius, Augustinus Ambrosius, Chrysostom and many others. (Laur: Theol. u. Gl. 1911, p. 445). In the Syriac Church it occurs as early as Ephraim (Edit. Romana t.II, pp. 1,2) and it is frequently found later on (Ishodad; Diettrich Beih.z. Z.A.W. VI, pp. XXII, XXIII, the Qarquphensiaus ... Theodor bar Koni, Script. Syr. Su. II, T. LXV, p. 336¹⁴, Bar Bahlul (sub. Job) Bar Hebraeus (introd. to Job), in a marginal note to Paris 9 (cf. Nan R.O.C. p. 261¹); Assemanus: Bibliothecae Apostolicae .... Vaticanae .... Catalogus II nr. VII etc.) The other view, that Job descended from Joqtan, is mentioned in Ishodadh, (loc.cit.) Bar Bahlul, (loc.cit.) Bar Hebraeus, (loc.cit.). Note on the margin of Paris 9 (loc.cit.) and nr. VII of Assemanni Catalogue (loc.cit.) Michael the Syrian (Chronicle Chapter 5) Theodor bar Koni (loc.cit.) The names we find in connection with this view are Asaph, Arwid, and Jacob of Edessa, so it seems likely that the latter introduced the theory in the Syriac exegesis. There we hear that God (not the angels) lifts the up by means of, or in, a cloud and carries them to certain regions where they are given as food for a strong people. The rather puzzling feeling with which one at first looks at this disappears when one realizes that what we have here is an attempt to explain the meteorological phenomenon which we call waterspouts. When a waterspout is formed the clouds seem to bulge downwards and the sea to rise until they meet in a huge pillar of rotating water. After some time the pillar breaks in the middle and the upper half remains for a short time hanging down from the clouds, in aspect not unlike the tail of a huge serpent. As we see from our text this was how the phenomenon actually was interpreted: A serpent that was lifted up into the clouds. Later on the verses Ps. 74.13-14 taken quite literally, were conceived as referring to this phenomenon and added the feature about the strong people. This explanation of the waterspouts is not peculiar to Bar Salibi; as far as I have been able to trace it the earliest occurrence is in Ishodadh's commentary on Job ad 40.23 where we probably have to read He takes it in his clouds, etc. He uses the Tannin as an example (those) which are lifted up in clouds and moved to desert places on God's suggestion in order not to trouble the world (mankind). Schliebitz reads for play and translates: Dies Beispiel handelt von den Drachen, die sich in die Wolken erheben and an einsamen Orten nach göttlichem Wink spielen, damit sie die Menschen nicht angreifen. Among the Moslems our story appears with Qazwini and ad-Damasqi. (Compare Lane's Dictionary sub ). It was probably borrowed from the Syrians.
